name: get_scene
title: Get scene
description: Returns the full scene graph: flat node dictionary, root node IDs, collections, and explicit installed plugin IDs when present.

name: validate_design
title: Validate design
description: Check a design (procedural item recipe) without changing the scene. Write it from pascal://schema/design (JSON Schema, rules and a valid example); a floor design has no mounting. Returns `valid`, coded `diagnostics` (errors block placement, warnings flag floating or unbalanced parts), the parameter `sweep`, and `measurements` at the given parameters: bounds, per-part bounds and instances, true triangle counts, draw groups per slot, datum contact and connected components. A design that does not match the schema gets every schema error at once, each with its `path`, what is `expected` there and what was `received`, plus `schemaUri` and a valid `example`: fix them all before calling again. Rules the schema cannot express are checked once it matches, each error with a `hint`. Version 2 designs validate fully but carry a design_version_not_enabled warning: placement accepts version 1 only until the next release.

design.description: The design (procedural recipe, version 1 or 2) as an object, or as a JSON string for clients that cannot send recursive objects. Schema: pascal://schema/design.

parameters.description: Parameter values to measure at, by parameter id. Defaults otherwise.

name: place_design
title: Place design
description: Create one instance of a design (procedural item recipe, object or JSON string) in the scene. The design must pass validate_design. Its mounting picks the host: floor designs go on a level (or a slab or zone of it) or on a named surface of a placed design; wall-side designs on a straight wall face; ceiling designs under a ceiling. Only creates: refusals carry a code (invalid_design with diagnostics, design_version_not_enabled for version 2 designs until the next release, design_too_large above 24 KiB, invalid_placement, node_exists, host_not_found, wrong_host, unknown_surface, does_not_fit) and change nothing.

design.description: The design (procedural recipe, version 1 or 2) as an object, or as a JSON string for clients that cannot send recursive objects. Schema: pascal://schema/design.

hostId.description: Floor designs: a level, or a slab or zone on it, or a placed design with surfaceId. Wall-side designs: a straight wall. Ceiling designs: a ceiling.

position.description: Metres. Floor: level-local [x, y, z], y above the floor. Wall-side: [along, height, offset] of the mounting reference from the wall start. Ceiling: plan [x, 0, z] of the reference. Surface: [x, 0, z] in the surface frame.

rotation.description: Yaw. Not for wall-side designs; use side to face the other way. In radians, or text with a unit ("90°").

side.description: Wall face for wall-side designs: front is the +normal side, normal (−Δz, Δx) of start→end. The wall's frontSide and backSide say which face is exterior (a facade light goes on that one).

surfaceId.description: Named surface of the host design to rest on (see validate_design measurements.surfaces).

parameters.description: Parameter values to measure at, by parameter id. Defaults otherwise.

slots.description: Slot id to "#rrggbb" or a scene:/library: material reference.

id.description: Optional new id ("procedural-item_…"). Refused if it exists: this tool only creates.

name: measure_stair
title: Measure stair
description: Inspect actual flight risers, walking-line going, slope, arrival, uniformity, headroom against floors, ceilings and stair bodies, and design-target diagnostics without changing measured geometry.

available.description: The space a new layout may take, to propose layouts that fit it.

width.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

length.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: fit_stair
title: Fit stair
description: Explicitly replace stair riser proportions with uniform risers from design targets. Optionally fit going by changing flight runs or arc sweep; preserves landing elevations. Optional straight, L or U layout replaces the flight chain with width-sized turning landings or quarter-turn winders. Winder going is measured along the selected walking line. One atomic edit.

width.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

landingDepth.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

innerGap.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

walkingLineOffset.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

maxRiserHeight.description: The tallest riser (default 0.18 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

minimumGoing.description: The shortest going (default 0.25 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

targetGoing.description: The going a fit aims for (default 0.28 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

minimumHeadroom.description: The least headroom over the flight (default 2 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: find_by_type
title: Find by type
description: Find every node, item, light or scripted part of one type in the scene, wherever it lives, and return the matches with their count. A type is a node kind (column, door, window, wall, stair, imported-mesh, a plugin's kind…), an item category, light (any item that emits light), or a part type inside scripted objects, windows and doors (a porch's columns, a window's grille). Narrow it to a level, a parent, a zone or an importer's source ids; without a type, every node the other filters match. A word that names nothing (no node kind, nor an item category or part type in this scene) is refused with the kinds the scene holds. Each result gives the node's id, name, kind, level and parent, with its metadata and provenance when it has them (one over 1 KB is named in omitted instead); get_node reads a node whole. Parts are read-only: they come back with their object's id, the part id and, for objects directly on a level, its bounds in level coordinates; edit them through their object. count says how many match; past limit (200 unless asked) the rest are left out of results, with truncated: narrow the call or raise limit.

type.description: What to find, one word: a node kind (wall, slab, imported-mesh, fixture:bench), an item category, light, or a part type (column, beam, panel, railing, trim…). Omit it to find every node the other filters match.

levelId.description: Only this level. Default: every level.

parentId.description: Only the nodes directly under this one: a wall's doors and windows, a roof's segments, a level's walls.

zoneId.description: Only what stands in this zone: on the zone's level, its plan point inside the zone's outline and outside its holes (a wall's midpoint, a polygon's centroid, a door or window where its wall puts it, a block or mesh by the middle of its geometry, a part with bounds by their middle).

sourceId.description: Only the nodes an importer recorded under this source id (provenance.refs[].id, or legacy metadata.sourceIds), exactly. Characters outside printable ASCII also match their percent-encoded form.

sourceIdPrefix.description: Only the nodes with a source id starting with this.

limit.description: How many results to list at most. Default 200; count still says how many match.

name: list_levels
title: List levels
description: List every level of every building in floor order: id, name, floorIndex, building (parentId), role (occupied storey, roof-only level or support level), child count, gradeStanding (at-grade, partly-below-grade or below-grade against the ground line and the terrain), isGroundLevel, and which one the person is viewing (isActive); groundLevels names, per building, the level at grade (levelId, whether the building names it, floorElevation, gradeElevation, floorOverGrade, seated). A roof-only level is the roof, not a storey.

name: get_node
title: Get node
description: Get the full data of any node by its id: its fields as stored, with what the scene decides for it beside them (a wall's or a ceiling's resolvedHeight, and heightIsExplicit, false when it follows its storey; a wall's resolvedThickness; a door's or window's resolvedOpening, its floor and what it hangs from; the displayName a level or a floor plate is shown by); its ancestorIds, its parent first (a door's wall, then the level, the building, the site); and the scene materials (scene:<id>) its finishes use. A container's node lists its children as stored; any that name no node are listed again in missingChildIds. A node its schema rejects comes back as stored, with nothing derived (verify_scene says what is wrong).

name: get_level_summary
title: Get level summary
description: Summarise one level so nothing on it goes unseen: its role and counts, then walls (length, heights, doors and windows), zones (name, area, size, floor_choices), slabs, ceilings, items (floor, wall and ceiling), floor openings, stairs, roofs, and anything else by type. Zone polygons: get_zones; a node's full data: get_node.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: get_walls
title: Get walls
description: Get the walls of a level: start and end in metres, length, stored and resolved height, thickness, wallType (standard, railing or curtain; standard when absent), type ({ id, label } for a known assembly preset or project wall type, null otherwise), and their doors and windows. wallTypes lists available assembly type ids and labels for add_wall.type and set_wall_type. wallFaceChains gives base-chain provenance for geometric faces a (left of start → end) and b (right): ref (authored face slot), legacy (inline spec), or default (declared fallback ref). These are not final rendered finishes: room intent, face paint regions, exterior assembly cladding and reference availability can change appearance. A chosen white or default-matching ref is legitimate; fallback alone is not a defect or a requirement to paint.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: get_zones
title: Get zones
description: Get the zones (rooms) of a level: name, colour, polygon and holes in metres, area in m² (holes taken out), bounding size, roomType (room when absent, porch, deck or patio), floor.drop (step-down in metres, 0 when absent; an explicit floor.elevation takes precedence), porchFraming (auto, postSize, postSpacing in metres, beamSize, postCount and beamCount of existing generated parts; null when no outdoor/framing intent), and decking (boardSize, gap in metres, direction; resolved defaults for decks or when settings exist). auto follows porchFraming.auto; absent, on for a covered porch, off for decks/patios. false leaves framing to hand edits. These names and units match set_zone_intent. Includes the unit it belongs to (unitId and unit, its name; null: common area), and floor_choices: available floor plates (key, plateId, name, current; drawn and mezzanine flags). A room shares its floor plate with adjacent rooms unless detached. Persisted wall intent is wallMaterial (string, null when absent) and wallOverrides (wallId, geometric face a or b, finish; [] when absent), not a final rendered finish: local overrides and face paint can take precedence; absent intent is not a defect or a requirement to paint.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: duplicate_level
title: Duplicate level
description: Copy a level with everything on it, as the editor does: fresh ids, internal links kept, and units whose rooms are all on that level copied too; plan references, scans and spawn points stay behind. The copy goes above the original (or below it) and the floors past it move up one.

levelId.description: The level to copy, by an id list_levels returned. Default: the floor the person is viewing.

position.description: Where the copy goes: above the original (default) or below it.

name.description: Name of the copy. Default: none, so it reads by its floor like a new level (Floor 1, Ground floor…).

preset.description: What to copy, as in the editor: everything (default); structure (walls, zones, slabs, ceilings, roofs, stairs, doors, windows) without materials; structure with its materials; or structure and furniture.

name: set_ground_level
title: Set ground level
description: Make a level the building's ground floor: the one standing at grade, its floor on the ground. A building's levels stack on a ground line; the levels with a lower floor index are below grade (basements), the ones at or over it are not, and list_levels reads it as groundLevels (levelId, floorElevation, floorOverGrade, seated) and each level's gradeStanding (at-grade, partly-below-grade, below-grade) and isGroundLevel. This names the level on the building, seats the building so that level's floor datum stands on grade (flat site: world Y 0; sculpted terrain: the mean ground height under its floor), moving the building in height only — the plan stays where it is and every level keeps its place relative to the others — and renumbers the floor indices so it is 0 and the ones under it are -1, -2…. A level added below (add_level position below) stacks under the lowest level without moving the ground floor. A roof level or a support level cannot be the ground floor (not_a_storey). One undo step. Refusals: level_not_found, not_a_level, no_building, not_a_storey. Answering unchanged: true when the level is already the named ground floor, on grade, at index 0.

levelId.description: The level to stand at grade, by an id list_levels returned.

name: verify_scene
title: Verify scene
description: Optional whole-scene evidence: per-level content, roles (storey, roof-only, support) and the spaces its walls enclose, then every problem found, each with a type: empty levels, walls with no room or door, a space the walls enclose with no room over it (space_no_room) or with several and no wall between them (space_many_rooms), a room the walls do not close (room_not_enclosed) or with no name (room_unnamed), two rooms on the same clear floor (zones_overlap) and floor inside a covered space that no zone or stair claims (floor_unclaimed), both warnings with their area, width and place and quiet under 0.1 m² (overlap), 0.3 m² (unclaimed) or 15 cm wide, wall bodies not counting as floor, an end that stops 3-25 cm short of another wall (wall_end_short, warning: the daylight in cm, both walls named; an end that touches a wall is a joint) and a wall 0.5-6 degrees off the line of the walls it carries on from or sits between, when that moves its far end 2 cm or more off the line (wall_nearly_aligned, warning: the angle, the offset, the neighbours; a larger turn is an angle drawn on purpose and is not named), rooms with no floor or ceiling, storeys with no stair, roof levels misused, walls intersecting a covering slab or ending coplanar with its walking surface (wall_covering_slab_contact, with wallId and slabId), openings off their wall, stairs off their slab or blocked, furniture blocking a door or overlapping, a house past its lot line or in its required yards, every node field its schema rejects (schema_invalid, with its nodeId and path; valid is then false, and the level holding the node lists it as unread and is measured once it is fixed), a node kind no schema here knows, once per kind (schema_unknown_kind, info: a plugin kind), a hidden site (site_hidden). What the surfaces of a room say, each one an observation to keep when it is intended: a wet room whose walls are not tiled where its fixtures stand (room_wet_untiled), skirting in no room or on part of the wall faces of a room (rooms_no_skirting, rooms_skirting_partial), and floors and wall faces left at the default finish (rooms_floors_default, wall_faces_default). Static authored ceiling objects report transformed bounds extending above their ceiling attachment and bounds overlapping solid covering slab bands, with node IDs and measured metres; stored and derived slab holes are subtracted. Wall-mounted objects report a front oriented toward their host; static authored wall bounds report wall-body overlap and extension through the opposite face. With settled editor meshes, catalog wall bounds and large competing coplanar faces against the host or another item on the same wall are also measured within 1 mm. Hidden back-to-wall contact is not competing face evidence. These are observations, not instructions to change the scene or proof of exact mesh intersection. Bounds are measured in the owning building frame, including stacked level elevations. Unknown catalog raw bounds without meshes, animated models, unsupported attachment frames, unresolved scripted wall cuts, roof collisions, recessed slab shells and foundation volumes are not assessed. Every warning and every error arrives whole, its own measurements with it; a repeated informational finding (severity info) arrives once, with its count, its elements and a few examples. Usage findings arrive trimmed, a narrow passage as one entry for the place with the rooms it leads to, each room's turning circle and pocket as one usage_room entry; `room` (a room's id or name) returns its whole findings plus every finding naming its items, doors or windows, even when placed in a neighbouring room; `type` returns the whole findings of that kind.

type.description: One finding type (for example "usage_passage_narrow"): the answer then lists every original finding of that type, whole, and none of the other blocks of the report.

room.description: A room's id or name: the answer lists its findings whole, including passages serving it and every finding naming its items, doors or windows.

name: set_checkpoint
title: Set a checkpoint
description: Name this moment of your work (a roof, a floor, a batch of walls) for verify_scene({ since: name }) to compare against, and return the checkpoints kept. verify_scene then lists what was created, changed and deleted since, grouped by level and kind with a view each, and what you made that is gone. "start", the beginning of your work, is always one; a name used again replaces the first; a session keeps at most 8. A checkpoint is kept with your session, not in the project: it changes nothing in the scene, enters no undo, and does not restore anything. Refused: too_many_checkpoints (naming them), scene_too_large, name_required.

name.description: A short name for this moment, e.g. "walls done" or "before roof".

name: design_brief
title: Write the design brief
description:
Record the request's design brief before furnishing, read axis by axis with a vision and where the objects come from, and return what it unlocks. It is written once for the whole request (piece by piece when the request invites it), each axis (action, size, form, facade, pieces, openings, style, materials, source, dressing) bounded by the person's own words or open with a design statement. It changes nothing in the scene.
Furnishings are placed or made after a brief: place_items, furnish_room, place_in_room (the catalog's) and add_object, place_design (the agent's own), also inside run_batch. Before one, search_assets and view_assets read the catalog and every other tool works as usual; rooms, walls, openings and finishes are not furnishings.
Bounded and open, in four readings. "a 4 by 5 m bedroom with a double bed, two nightstands, a wardrobe, one window, one door": action, size, form, facade, pieces (as a minimum: those pieces must be there, more may come) and openings bounded, the form and the facade by "a 4 by 5 m bedroom" (one room, no building designed); style, materials, source and dressing open. "add a lamp next to the sofa": action, form, facade and dressing bounded by "add a lamp" (one object in a room that exists, the building and its exterior stand as they are); style open, its design statement saying how this lamp is designed. "a bedroom with only a bed and a lamp": form and facade bounded by "a bedroom", pieces exact and dressing bounded by "only a bed and a lamp"; style and materials open, the bed and the lamp designed, not defaulted. "Build a house": the action bounded only by "a house"; every other axis open, the form, the facade and the dressing included, and rooms with an entry for each room.
source open: technical equipment (sanitaryware, kitchen, laundry and climate appliances) and plants are placed from the catalog (place_items, place_in_room), every other catalog piece is made (add_object, place_design), and furnish_room, which places a whole stock set, stays closed. source catalog, brand or existing: place_items, furnish_room and place_in_room are open, and the creation tools stay open for what the catalog lacks.
The form is the building's massing: a plan shape, a number of volumes, and whether the volumes stand at different heights. Open, its design statement says how the building is composed and massing states it: plan (polygon, rectangle, l, u, t, h, courtyard, wing, bay, detached), volumes (a count) and heights (one or several). Bounded, the person's own words fix the form ("an L-shaped house", "a single-storey bungalow") and massing may state what they fix; a request that builds or changes no building bounds it by its own words, the building standing as it is.
The facade is the exterior identity of the building: its materials, the bands and elements it carries, the rhythm of its openings. Open, its design statement says how the exterior is designed and treatment states it: cladding (brick, stone, render, siding, wood, metal), bands (base, course, cornice), elements (corners, surrounds, shutters, balconies, entrance, curtain-wall, porch, guard, posts) and rhythm (regular or free: openings stacked storey over storey, or placed one by one). Bounded, the person's own words fix the facade ("une façade en pierre avec volets", "a black timber-clad house") and treatment may state what they fix; a request that builds or changes no building exterior bounds it by its own words, the exterior standing as it is.
rooms lists the rooms the request builds or refits, when it builds or refits more than one (a single-room request or a focused edit carries none; an open form owes them): for each, name (as the scene names the room), use (bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, living, dining, office, hallway, laundry, garage, other), distinct (one line: what sets the room apart from the other rooms of its use, who it is for and its character), finishes (floor and walls as short phrases, tiled and skirting as true or false, and dressing when its walls are dressed) and pieces (its main pieces: furniture, fixtures, equipment). Rooms of the same use are distinct rooms, each with its own distinct line.
Naming a piece (a double bed) states its function; its form, size within reason and finish are open unless the request fixes them. The pieces a request names are what the room must contain, not all it may contain: where the dressing axis is open, beyond states that design layer by layer: textiles, light, windows, walls, floor, plants, objects, small furniture, each a list of pieces or { none: why }, at least 6 of the 8 layers naming pieces; where the dressing is bounded (words that limit the pieces or the action, such as "only", "nothing else", "just"), none in every layer is accepted. The pieces the request names, read as a minimum, do not bound the dressing. The answer hands the pieces back as dressing.
A source other than open is set by the request, not chosen: sourceQuote holds the person's own words that name it, at least two words naming a brand (the brief's brand), the catalog or what is already there ("IKEA furniture only", "que du catalogue", "use my existing furniture"); a request that names no source is open.
The next design_brief replaces the brief in force. Refused: axis_missing (an axis other than form and facade is absent), axis_quote_not_in_request (a bounded axis's quote is not in the person's message), axis_open_without_design (an open axis without a design statement of at least 3 words), form_massing_missing (an open form without its massing: plan, volumes, heights), form_massing_inconsistent (one volume stated as detached or at several heights), facade_treatment_missing (an open facade without its treatment: cladding or elements, and rhythm), rooms_missing (an open form with no rooms), room_distinct_missing (a room without its distinct line), rooms_identical (two rooms of one use with the same distinct and the same pieces), dressing_bounded_by_minimum (the dressing bounded by words inside a pieces quote read as a minimum), brand_required (source brand without a brand name), source_quote_required (a source other than open without sourceQuote), source_not_named (the quote names no brand, catalog or existing source), source_not_in_request (the quote is not in the person's message), beyond_too_thin (dressing open, fewer than 6 layers naming pieces).
There is no person's message here: a source quote must still name its source, and no quote is compared with a request. A brief lasts for the session.

name: add_wall
title: Add wall
description: Add a single wall between two points on a level, straight or, with curveOffset, an arc. type applies a preset or project wall assembly including its thickness (unknown_wall_type for an unknown id). wallType railing builds the Build panel guard: default post-and-rail, 0.9144 m high, thickness from railing.postSize, no assembly or foundation. Its doors are gaps; windows refuse railing_window, skirting refuses railing_wall. railing settings on a standard wall refuse not_a_railing; type on a railing refuses railing_wall. Refused with a code: a level that is not a storey (a declared roof level), and a wall shorter than 1 cm. On a level below grade, a standard wall against the ground (on the outline of the walls of the level) is a foundation wall, built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read; a partition inside the outline is an ordinary wall; the result says which.

start.description: [x, z] start point in level coordinates (metres).

end.description: [x, z] end point in level coordinates (metres).

type.description: Assembly type id from get_walls.wallTypes: a built-in preset or custom- project wall type. Copies its layers and total thickness in metres, overriding thickness. Unknown ids: unknown_wall_type.

style.description: Guard style (default post-and-rail); omitted member sizes use the style defaults from the Build panel.

thickness.description: Wall thickness (default 0.1 m; a wall against the ground on a level below grade, given none, is a foundation wall built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read; a partition inside it is an ordinary wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Wall height (default: the storey's height; a railing 0.9144 m / 36 in). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

curveOffset.description: Bends the wall into an arc: the sagitta, from the middle of the straight line start→end to the middle of the arc. Positive bows the middle toward the back face (the −normal side, normal (−Δz, Δx) of start→end), the arc's centre on the front side; negative the other way. At most half the chord (a half circle); more is clamped. A quarter round of radius r at a corner: end both walls r short of the corner and join their ends with an arc of curveOffset ±0.293·r, the sign that bows it outward. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: set_wall_type
title: Set wall type
description: Apply an assembly type to existing standard walls, copying its layers and total thickness as the wall panel does. type null clears the assembly and keeps thickness. All walls change together. Refused with unknown_wall_type for an unknown type id, target_not_found for a missing wall, curtain_wall or railing_wall for walls that take no assembly.

name: add_fence
title: Add fence
description: Add a fence along points on a level: one fence per side, a whole run or a lot's boundary (closed) in one call. Privacy (solid panels) by default; picket for a picket fence, slat for vertical slats, rail for open rails, horizontal for cladding boards, guard for a deck's barrier. Fences stand on the level, as the editor's fence tool puts them. Refused with a code: a side shorter than 10 cm (fence_too_short), a roof level (roof_level).

points.description: [x, z] points in level coordinates (metres), the fence running through them in order.

closed.description: Close the run back to the first point, as a lot's boundary.

height.description: Fence height (default 1.8 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

style.description: slat | rail | privacy | horizontal | guard | picket (default privacy).

baseStyle.description: grounded (default: a kickboard on the ground), floating (the panel held off the ground on its posts) or raised (a bottom rail held above the ground, the posts to the ground: a deck guard).

materialPreset.description: A library material (library:<id>), found with search_materials.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: add_corner_window
title: Add corner window
description: Add a window that wraps the corner where two walls meet, one window on each wall joined at the corner, and return their windowIds and wallIds. Both run to the corner, the glass fused there (post none, a fixed window's default) or meeting at a thin post (post post). Any angle the walls make, a bay's 135° as well as a square or an acute corner. The corner is the point the two walls end at ([x, z], as get_walls gives their ends); width is how far the glass runs along each wall from the corner, the same on both unless widths names a wall. Each side is placed by add_window's rules (height, sillHeight, windowType, style the same on both sides; with no sillHeight, centred on the lower of the two walls). The walls are the level's (levelId, default the floor the person is viewing): stacked storeys share their corners' points. Refused with a code: no_corner where no two walls of the level end at the point, corner_ambiguous where more than two do (name two with wallIds), corner_angle for a corner nearly folded back or nearly straight, corner_not_fused for post none on a window type other than fixed, width_exceeds_wall. The editor's window panel shows the pair under Corner.

corner.description: The point where the two walls meet, [x, z] in the level's plan (m).

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

wallIds.description: The two walls, when more than two end at the corner.

width.description: How far the glass runs along each wall from the corner (default 1.2 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

widths.description: A width for a wall by its id, over width (e.g. { "wall_a": 1.6 }).

additionalProperties.description: The side on that wall. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the lower of the two walls, the same on both sides). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

post.description: none: the glass fused at the corner (a fixed window's default); post: the glass meets at a thin post (the default, and the only choice, for the other window types, whose frames stay).

windowType.description: How it opens (default fixed), the window panel's Type row; the fused corner is a fixed window's.

style.description: The panes' look on each side (rows and columns), the window panel's Style row.

name: merge_windows
title: Merge windows
description: Make two windows that exist one window, as the editor's Merge windows does: nothing is recreated. On two walls that meet at a corner, each window within 0.30 m of that corner, they become one corner window (the add_corner_window result): each is slid to the corner keeping its width, the glass fused (post none), and both take the first window's height, sill and type, so name first the window whose look you want; the corner is refused over 170° or under 10° (walls_not_meeting, corner_angle, window_not_at_corner, height_exceeds_wall). On one wall, two windows with at most 0.30 m between them and nothing between become one window spanning both outer edges, from the lower sill to the higher head, with the first window's type and style (windows_not_adjacent, opening_between). Refused with a code and a sentence that says why: window_not_found, not_a_window, same_window, window_not_on_wall, window_already_joined (unwrap it first), windows_already_joined, opening_overlap (sliding to the corner would land on another opening). Returns kind (corner or same_wall), the windows that stay (windowIds) and the one that went (removedIds). Use it for two windows already built that open a corner or one wide opening; add_corner_window builds a new pair, and verify_scene's corner_unjoined names two windows this joins.

windowIds.description: The two windows, the one whose height, sill and type the result keeps named first.

name: add_level
title: Add level
description: Add an empty level to a building as the editor does, above its top storey or below its lowest for a basement, and return its id, floor index and height. Above, it goes under the building's roof level, which moves up one so the roof stays on top; a basement goes one storey under the lowest level, every existing level keeping its place, the ground floor included. On a scene with no building (a new or cleared scene), it starts the scene as the editor does: a site, a building and its ground level. A level that ends up below grade says in its result how a new wall on it is built (wallConstruction): a wall against the ground is a foundation wall, built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read, a partition is an ordinary wall. To copy a floor with its content, use duplicate_level.

buildingId.description: The building. Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

position.description: above (default): over the top storey, under the roof level; below: under the lowest, a basement.

height.description: Floor-to-floor storey height (default 2.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: create_stair
title: Create stair
description:
Create a straight, L or U staircase rising from a level, as the editor's stair tool builds one, and return its id, its footprint and where the top step arrives. An L is a flight, a landing as deep as the stair is wide and a flight turned 90°; a U is a flight, a landing across and a flight back beside the first. It rises to the level above and owns the floor opening it cuts in every floor it passes; when no level stands above, a blank one is made for it. toLevelId null makes a flight to no level (porch steps, a deck, a raised platform): it rises height, cuts nothing and makes no level. Refused with a code: a flight to or from a declared roof level, and a toLevelId that is not above the level it rises from.

GEOMETRY (get this wrong and the stair pokes through a wall):
- (x, z) is the middle of the bottom riser, where the flight starts. The first flight runs from there along the climb: at rotation 0 it covers x − width/2 .. x + width/2 and z .. z + its run.
- rotation in degrees about Y: 0 climbs toward +Z, 90 → +X, 180 → −Z, 270 → −X. Point the climb into the room, away from the wall the bottom step sits against.
- An L or U turns to the climber's left or right (turn). The result gives the whole footprint and the point the top step arrives at.
- Keep 0.9 m clear at the foot and at the head of the flight, and the whole footprint inside one room on both levels (a hall is typical): read the room's outline first (get_zones).

OPENINGS: by default the stair owns the opening over its flights and keeps it as the stair moves (openingOffset widens it). An opening of another size, centre or turn, through a slab or ceiling you name, or through one of the two only, is cut as an opening the stair owns, as given.

x.description: X of the middle of the bottom riser.

z.description: Z of the middle of the bottom riser.

rotation.description: The first flight's climb (default 0 = toward +Z; 90 = +X, 180 = −Z, 270 = −X). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

layout.description: straight (default); l: a flight, a landing, a flight turned 90°; u: a flight, a landing across, a flight back beside the first.

turn.description: Which way an L or U turns, to the climber's left or right (default left).

lowerSteps.description: An L or U's risers in the first flight; the rest are in the last (default half).

width.description: Side-to-side width, across the climb (default 1.0 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

length.description: The flights' horizontal run along the climb, landings aside (default: from the stair's design targets, 0.28 m of going per riser, risers of at most 0.18 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Vertical rise. Omit it unless asked for a specific rise: the flight then follows the storey's floor-to-floor height and keeps tracking it. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

steps.description: Number of risers in all. Omit it to derive ~18 cm risers from the rise; pass it when the run was planned from a step count.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

toLevelId.description: The level the flight arrives on. Default: the next level above, created when there is none. null: a flight to no level, rising height (default the storey's floor-to-floor height).

railingMode.description: Which sides have a railing, looking up the flight (default both).

railingStyle.description: How the railings are built (default balusters): post-and-rail, cable (contemporary with a black railingMaterial), boards, glass or metal.

railingMaterial.description: A library material for the railings (library:<id>); an unknown one is refused.

materialPreset.description: A library material for the flight (library:<id>); an unknown one is refused.

createDestinationSlabOpening.description: Cut the floor it arrives through (default true).

createSourceCeilingOpening.description: Cut the ceiling of the floor it leaves (default true).

destinationSlabId.description: The slab it arrives through. Default: the floor of the level it arrives on.

sourceCeilingId.description: The ceiling it rises through. Default: the ceiling of the level it leaves.

openingWidth.description: The opening across the climb (default the stair's footprint). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

openingLength.description: The opening along the climb (default the stair's footprint). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

openingOffset.description: A margin round the opening on every side (default 0.08 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

openingCenter.description: The opening centre (x, z). Default: the middle of the stair's footprint.

openingRotation.description: The opening's turn (default the stair's). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

name: create_roof
title: Create roof
description: Cap a storey with a roof over its footprint (its walls' outline, else its floor plates, else its rooms), swept in the building's own axes into rectangles, one roof segment each. Without a roofType: a gable for one rectangle, hips for a few wings, flat for a large block. The roof goes on the building's roof level above the top storey (the empty level directly above when it is the only one; made, named Roof, when there is none), and stands on the storey's wall tops, so exploded and solo level views lift it off the plan. Glazed construction supports gable, straight shed and barrel. Barrel depth is the span; barrelRise is at most half the span. glazing controls frame, glass, grids and panels. Paint glazing-frame, glazing-glass or glazing-solid. Call it once the storeys and their exterior walls stand. Refused with a code: storey_above (another storey stands above: a roof caps the top one; a lower wing's roof is drawn with the Roof tool), building_required (no level named on a site of several buildings: pass a level of the one to roof), roof_exists (the storey already has a roof: edit it, or delete_node it first when the person asked for a new one), no_rooms (no rooms or closed walls on any level of the building: pass width and depth to roof a rectangle of your own).

spacing.description: Bar spacing, for the maximum-spacing and fixed-spacing layouts. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Range 0.2–100 m.
Bar spacing, for the maximum-spacing and fixed-spacing layouts. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Range 0.2–100 m.

frameDepth.description: Frame bar depth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

glassThickness.description: Glass pane thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

barrelRise.description: Barrel arch rise, at most half each segment span. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Roof wall thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.
