roofType.description: The shape of every segment. Default: chosen from the footprint.

pitch.description: Slope of the roof planes (default 40°). In degrees, or rise over run ("6:12"). Range 0–85 deg.

overhang.description: Eave overhang: how far the eaves reach past the walls in plan (a segment stores it along its slope). Read it from the photo: a deep modern overhang is 1–2 m. Default 0.3. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

wallHeight.description: Knee walls under the eaves (default 0: the roof starts at the wall tops). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

width.description: With depth: roof a rectangle of your own instead of the footprint (a wing, or walls drawn without rooms), along x. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

depth.description: The rectangle's depth, along z. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

center.description: The rectangle's centre [x, z] in metres (default [0, 0]).

materialPreset.description: The roof finish, a library material.

fasciaHeight.description: A fascia band of that height round the roof's eaves and rakes; on a flat roof it reaches the roof's top, a coping over its edge. Absent (and no fasciaMaterialPreset): no band. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

fasciaMaterialPreset.description: The band's finish, a library material (a black fascia: library:preset-nearblack); the roof's wall finish when absent.

name.description: What the user would call it (default "Roof").

name: move_roofs_to_roof_level
title: Move roofs to the roof level
description: Move the roofs a storey holds on its own walls to the level the roof rule gives them, and return the roofs moved and the level they went to. It does what a roof's panel does by hand (Move to the roof level): over the top storey, the building's roof level (made, named Roof, when there is none); under an upper storey, that storey. Each roof stands exactly where it stood, its segments, finishes and id kept: only the level holding it changes, so exploded and solo level views show the storey's plan with no roof over it. For a project built before roofs had their own level, when verify_scene reports roof_mixed_in_storey. Refused with a code: level_not_found, no_roof_on_walls (the storey holds no roof standing on its walls; a porch roof on its beam and a lower wing's roof on the storey above already sit where they belong). Returns the roofs moved (roofIds), the level they went to (roofLevelId) and the roof level made for them (createdRoofLevelId).

levelId.description: The storey whose roofs move, by an id list_levels returned.

name: place_items
title: Place items
description: Place one or more catalog items (furniture, fixtures, plants, art, lights) in one call. Each assetId is a known catalog id, available from search_assets results or existing scene item data, never guessed. Positions are level (x, z) metres. An item stands on the floor of the level, or on the host it names (targetNodeId): a wall (art, a sconce: y is the height of its bottom above the floor, required; it goes on the side of the wall the point is on), a ceiling (a pendant, a downlight: it hangs flush under it), or an item standing on the floor (a lamp on a nightstand: it rests on its top; on an object built with add_object it rests on the real surface under the point, such as a porch landing, or a ceiling item hangs from the underside above it, such as a sloped vault, and the result names it in restingOn). A room, a slab or a level as the target means its floor. Each item is placed or refused on its own (asset_not_found; outside_rooms: an indoor item on the floor outside every room of a level that has rooms — garden and outdoor items may stand outside; height_required, item_too_tall, unsupported_host, host_not_found, host_not_on_level; blocks_door: a floor item standing where a door needs space, with a spot in its room that clears every door; too_large_for_room: a floor item its room cannot hold in any turn).

assetId.description: A known catalog id; search_assets can find it.

y.description: Height above the floor (metres): on a wall, of the item's bottom (required: art centred at eye level is 1.5 − its height / 2, a sconce about 1.5); on an item, a resting height you set rather than its top. Not used on a floor or a ceiling.

targetNodeId.description: The host: a wall, a ceiling or an item standing on the floor; a room, a slab or a level means its floor. Default: the level's floor.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical (default 0). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: delete_node
title: Delete node
description: Delete a node with everything under it, as the editor's Delete does: a wall goes with its doors and windows, a level with everything on it. The floors above a deleted level keep their index.

name: move_node
title: Move node
description: Move one node as the editor's move tool does, re-seated on its wall, ceiling, roof segment or level, and return where it now sits and whether it clamped. A door, window or wall item slides along its wall (the plan point is projected onto the wall, clamped to stay on it, and refused with opening_overlap where it would hit a sibling, unless force, like holding Alt); a ceiling item moves in plan under its ceiling, keeping its drop; a floor or free node moves in plan on its level, keeping its height; a roof piece (skylight, chimney, vents, solar, dormer) moves in its segment-local plan, the frame its stored position uses, its height staying anchored to the segment surface; a wall takes by only (its ends translate, its openings ride in their wall-local seats). to and by are plan metres [x, z]: level plan for level, wall and ceiling hosts, segment-local for a roof host. Exactly one of to (absolute) or by (delta), or rotation alone. y is a window's sill height or a wall item's bottom height in metres, and nothing else takes it. rotation is yaw in degrees for free, ceiling and roof nodes. Returns the host class and id, the node's stored position after the move (a wall: its start point as [x, 0, z]), and whether the seat clamped. Refusals: node_not_found, node_not_movable (site, building, level, zone — use move_zone — roof, roof segment, stair, derived plates and other geometry-defined kinds), move_target_required, move_target_ambiguous (both to and by, or to on a wall), move_host_missing (its wall, ceiling or segment is gone), curved_wall, wall_too_short, wall_too_low, opening_overlap, rotation_not_supported (wall-hosted nodes face their wall side), height_not_applicable, move_not_supported (an item resting on another item).

to.description: Absolute plan target [x, z] in metres, in the frame the description names for its host.

by.description: Plan delta [dx, dz] in metres from where the node sits, same frame as to.

y.description: A window's sill height or a wall item's bottom height above the floor, in metres.

rotation.description: Yaw in degrees (free, ceiling and roof nodes).

force.description: Allow a wall seat that overlaps a sibling, like holding Alt in the editor.

name: duplicate_node
title: Duplicate node
description: Duplicate nodes with everything under them, as the editor's Duplicate does, and return each copy's id beside its source's. The copies get fresh ids, hosted children are re-hosted on them (a wall brings its doors, windows and wall items, their wallId pointing at the copy), and an id inside another listed subtree is skipped rather than copied twice. A door, window, wall item, ceiling item or roof piece copied on its own stays on its same host. offset [dx, dz] in plan metres moves every copy from its source's seat (default [0, 0], an exact copy in place, as the editor's duplicate starts); a wall offset translates its ends, a hosted copy's offset slides it on its host, clamped to stay seated. targetLevelId puts level-parented copies on that level instead; a hosted copy refuses it (hosted_root_level) because its host stays behind. Returns copies (sourceId, copyId, type, descendantCount), totalCreated and skippedIds. Refusals: node_not_found, duplicate_not_supported (a site, building, level — use duplicate_level — zone — use duplicate_zone — roof or roof segment, or a derived plate), duplicate_root_invalid (a node the editor only copies as part of its parent), hosted_root_level, level_not_found.

ids.description: The node ids to copy, each with everything under it.

offset.description: Plan delta [dx, dz] in metres applied to every copy. Default [0, 0].

targetLevelId.description: Copy level-parented roots onto this level instead of their own.

name: create_room
title: Create room
description: Create a room on a level from its polygon: a wall per edge, an edge a wall already runs along reusing that wall (rooms share their boundary with their neighbour), and the room zone that names it. The floor plate and the ceiling are derived from the room — never author a slab or a ceiling for it. Declare the room's doors and windows in the same call by polygon edge (wallIndex) and t along it, no wall ids needed; each is placed with add_door's and add_window's rules, and one that cannot be is skipped and listed in skippedOpenings with its code. Returns zoneId, slabId, ceilingId, wallIds in edge order (null where no wall), doorIds, windowIds. outdoor: true draws a terrace instead: separators where no wall runs, no walls of its own and no ceiling. Where the walls already enclose a room the reconciler numbered, the call names that room instead of adding a second one; where they enclose a room with a name of its own (not a number the editor gave it), it is refused (room_named_by_person) unless rename is true, which you pass only when the person asked for the rename, so a name is never changed silently. Not available in run_batch: the result needs the floor plate and ceiling derived by the host after reconciliation.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The corners in order, as [x, z] in metres.

color.description: Hex colour of the room zone, e.g. "#22c55e"; omit it and the room gets a palette colour picked from its id.

wallHeight.description: Omit to follow the storey and covering-slab underside. Equal to the stored storey height also follows that plane; other values are body heights above the wall's support, including deliberately taller walls. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Thickness of the walls it builds. Omitted, a wall against the ground on a level below grade is a foundation wall built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read, a partition inside the outline is an ordinary wall; a thickness keeps the schema wall. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rename.description: Only where the walls already enclose a room with a name of its own (not a number the editor gave it): true names that room with `name` instead of the refusal room_named_by_person. Pass it only when the person asked for the rename; otherwise ask them first.

outdoor.description: true for an outdoor room (a terrace): closed with separators (the editor's Separator: a room boundary with no wall) where no wall runs, no walls of its own and no ceiling.

doors.description: The entry door and the doors to the rooms next to it.

wallIndex.description: The polygon edge it sits on: edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1.

t.description: Position along that edge: 0 = its start, 1 = its end (default 0.5).

sidelightLeft.description: Fixed glazed light left of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sidelightRight.description: Fixed glazed light right of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

transomHeight.description: Fixed light above a swing door and its sidelights, metres; absent or 0 means none. The full cutout must fit under the wall top (wall_too_low). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

slidingStyle.description: Sliding family: patio (default) or two-track bypass closet.

width.description: Door width (default 0.9 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Door height (default 2.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

swingDirection.description: Which way the door opens (default inward).

style.description: Visual preset: 'panel' (default raised-panel), 'glass' (mostly glass), 'modern' (flush slab), 'paneled-glass' (glass top, panel bottom — an entry door), 'french' (two narrow glass leaves), 'shaker' (one flat panel), 'six-panel' (3 × 2 traditional grid), 'craftsman' (4 stacked vertical panels), 'half-louvered' (slats on top, panel below — closet, laundry), 'barn' (wide recessed panel). One style per room type across the home; the entry door may differ.

windows.description: Windows, on exterior edges only: not on an edge shared with another room.

wallIndex.description: The polygon edge it sits on: edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1.

t.description: Position along that edge: 0 = its start, 1 = its end (default 0.5).

hingesSide.description: Casement or tilt-turn side hinges (default left).

openingDirection.description: Casement or awning swing toward exterior or interior, independent of placement (new windows default outward). Ignored by hopper and tilt-turn, which open inward.

tiltTurnMode.description: Tilt-turn only: tilt inward about the bottom up to 15 degrees (default), or turn inward about the side hinges up to 90 degrees.

rollerShutter.description: Roller mount (default none): box on the exterior face above the opening, or concealed with a 0.03 m lintel strip and 0.025 x 0.03 m guides inside the reveal. Concealed curtain sits 0.02 m outside the frame plane, width minus 0.05 m.

rollerShutterBoxHeight.description: Exterior roller box height (default 0.18 m); used only by the box mount. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rollerShutterOpen.description: Static roller curtain position: 0 down, 1 fully up (default 1), independent of operationState.

shutterOpen.description: Exterior shutter position: 0 closed over the window, 1 open (default 1). Leaves over 0.75 m fold into two stacked halves; narrower leaves open flat against the wall.

shutterSides.description: Which exterior shutter leaves to build (default both).

sillOverhang.description: Exterior sill extension on each side; default 0.4 times sillDepth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sillInteriorDepth.description: Interior stool depth (default 0.06 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorThickness.description: Interior stool thickness (default 0.03 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorOverhang.description: Interior stool extension beyond casing on each side (default 0.015 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

columns.description: Panes across each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal widths; overrides the style's panes.

rows.description: Panes up each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal heights; overrides the style's panes.

windowHandle.description: Show the interior sash handle (default true).

sashGrid.description: Pane grid per operable sash (default false; columns or rows enable it).

sillInterior.description: Add a stool board on the room side (default false).

shutters.description: Exterior shutters (default none), with a 10 mm overlap lip on one leaf when both sides are present.

shutterWidth.description: Width per side, uncapped: defaults to half the opening for both sides, full opening for left or right only. Widths over 0.75 m form a bifold pair of equal halves. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

width.description: Window width (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

style.description: Visual preset: 'single' (default single pane), 'double-hung', 'triple-hung' (stacked sashes), 'casement' (two panes side by side), 'sliding' (three side by side — wide), 'grid' (2 × 2), 'tall-grid' (2 × 3), 'wide-grid' (3 × 2), 'horizontal-bands' (4 stacked bands), 'transom' (a small row over a larger pane), 'picture' (an alias of 'single'). One style for all the windows of a room, and per room type across the home.

name: furnish_room
title: Furnish room
description: Place the catalog's fixed furniture set for a room type: one set per type, not matched to a style. The bed, sofa, counters or toilet go against the wall facing the door, the rest along a side wall, each set off its wall by its own depth. Name the room by zoneId (its level and outline come with it), or give its polygon and level. The door wall is the edge a door of the room stands on, else doorWallIndex, else edge 0. Nothing lands in a door's clear zone or on another item: a piece that does not fit is nudged, else skipped, and skipped says why. Items stand on the room's level. The set per room type: bedroom: double-bed (a side of 3.2 m or more) or single-bed, two bedside-table, dresser (10 m² or more), closet (13 m² or more); kitchen: kitchen (back wall of 2.6 m or more) or kitchen-counter, stove (back wall of 3.5 m or more), fridge; bathroom: toilet, bathroom-sink, bathtub (6.5 m² or more) or shower-square; living: sofa, coffee-table, livingroom-chair, tv-stand; dining: dining-table, two dining-chair (four when both sides are 3 m or more); laundry: washing-machine, drying-rack; entry and hallway: coat-rack (both sides 1.4 m or more); storage: closet. The result lists each piece placed with its size and id, and each piece skipped with its reason. view_scene with interior { zoneId } shows the room from inside, at a person's height.

zoneId.description: The room: zoneId from create_room, or an id from get_zones.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The room's corners as [x, z] in metres, when there is no zoneId.

doorWallIndex.description: The polygon edge (i → i + 1) to treat as the door wall: for a room with no door yet, or to override the one found.

name: paint
title: Paint
description: Give walls, slabs, ceilings, roofs, columns, fences, doors, windows, stairs, blocks, cabinets, shelves, items and the other built parts a finish in one call, as the editor's Paint does. Give one finish: color (#rrggbb, painted with the nearest of the library's flat colours, said with how near; with exact: true, that colour itself, a matte scene material); material, a library:<id> (find it with search_materials) or scene:<id> ref, or a native material {properties: {color, roughness, metalness}} for an exact finish, kept as a scene material (materialName names a new one) and reused when the scene holds an equal one; or erase: true, back to the surface's default. role picks the surface: a wall's face a or b, or exterior and interior (the faces turned out of its rooms or into them, else by its stored sides; a partition is interior on both; a wall whose sides are unknown, or with rooms along only part of a face, is refused: name its face, a or b), its trims aSkirting, bSkirting, aCrown, bCrown, aChairRail, bChairRail (skirting, crown or chairRail: that trim on both faces), a curtain wall's curtain-frame, curtain-glass, curtain-solid; a slab's surface, side, edge, riser, underside or foundation; a ceiling's surface; a roof's top (the covering), edge (the gable ends and the trim band), wall (the soffit and the deck edge, and the fascia and rake boards unless they have their own) or fascia (the fascia and rake boards, a fascia band); a glazed roof's glazing-frame, glazing-glass or glazing-solid; a column's shaft, base, capital or frame; a fence's posts, infill, base or rail; a door's panel, frame, glass or hardware; a window's frame, glass, hardware or shutters; a stair's treads, body or railing; a block's body; a cabinet's front, carcass, countertop, plinth, hardware or glass; another part's own slots, which a refusal names; an item's surfaces by the names its model gives them (its painted ones are in get_node's slots), which paint cannot check. Without a role: both faces of a wall, a slab's or a ceiling's surface, a roof's top, a glazed roof's frame and solid panels, a column's shaft, a whole fence, a door's panel and frame, a window's frame, a block's body, a part's one surface. A roof shows one finish per surface: a segment's finish goes on its roof, and a roof's on all of its segments. A glazed segment holds its own glazing finishes: a roof's glazing roles go on its glazed segments, its other roles on the roof, and without a role both. A wall face is painted whole, over the wall finish of the room it faces; its painted parts keep their own, named in the note. A ceiling shows its finish's colour, not its texture. The result says the finish written, and the scene material when there is one. A target that is not in the scene, a role it lacks or an unknown material refuses the whole call: nothing is painted.

color.description: A colour, #rrggbb: painted with the nearest library colour, or as given with exact.

exact.description: With color: paint that colour itself, a matte scene material, not the nearest library colour (a brand colour, a colour matched to a photo).

material.description: A library:<id> or scene:<id> ref, or a native material kept as a scene material: properties color, roughness, metalness; texture { url (https, or artifact://<sha256> of an image stored with the project), repeat [u, v] (tiles per metre), offset [u, v] (in tiles), normalMap, normalScale, bumpMap, bumpScale }, its maps sharing the image's repeat and offset. Surfaces are laid in level metres: a floor, a slab's top or a ceiling at u = plan x, v = −z; a wall face at u = x for a wall running along x (−x on its face turned to −z), z for one running along z (−z on its face turned to −x), v = 1 − the height above the level's floor. A joint at c along u or v: offset = frac(−c × repeat).

materialName.description: The name of a new native material; an equal one already in the scene keeps its own.

name: place_in_room
title: Place an item in a room
description: Put one floor-standing catalog item in a room where it fits, without working out a position. Wall/ceiling-attached assets need a host: place_items accepts targetNodeId and, for a wall, y for the bottom height. A wall-bound floor piece (fridge, counter, stove, sink, TV stand, dresser, wardrobe, sofa, bed, bedside table, toilet, bath, shower, bookcase, cabinet) stands against a wall, centred in the widest free stretch of that wall (clear of every door and every other item), its front toward the room; it is never put in the middle, and when no wall has room the answer says how wide the widest free stretch is. A free-standing piece (dining table, rug, coffee table, plant, armchair) takes the middle of the room, or goes with what it belongs with: a coffee table and an armchair face the sofa. A chair goes around its table, one call per chair, facing the table, and is refused when the room has no table. Explicit edge, align, offset or inset instead requests a wall free run for any floor piece. Name the room by its zoneId (create_room, get_zones), or by its polygon and level. The item is a catalog id from search_assets. To furnish a whole room by its type in one call, use furnish_room.

assetId.description: A known catalog id; search_assets can find it.

zoneId.description: The room: zoneId from create_room, or an id from get_zones.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The room's corners as [x, z] in metres, when there is no zoneId.

edge.description: Stand it against this polygon edge (i → i + 1) instead of the best one.

rotationDeg.description: World yaw in degrees, overriding the automatic inward, group or table-facing yaw. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

facing.description: In by default. Out adds 180 degrees after any explicit rotationDeg.

align.description: Desired wall alignment, clamped into a valid free run. Defaults to the widest run’s center.

offset.description: Signed metres along the wall from the desired alignment; defaults to zero. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

inset.description: Normal gap in metres between the rotated footprint and the wall centerline; defaults to 0.1 m. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

clearanceAreas.description: Existing clearance rectangles, in world metres, to keep free before placing.

allowDuplicate.description: Place it even though the room already has this item. Off by default (a second toilet or stove is a mistake); chairs are always allowed.

name: get_site
title: Get site
description: Read the site a building stands on and return, in its level coordinates, its lot, buildable area, street side, north, ground and the footprint's yards. It gives the lot and its area, with the footprint a house usually covers on it (30 to 45%); the buildable area inside the setbacks with its centre, its area, each edge's frontage and depth, and its front edge (behind the street; while no street is recorded, behind the edge facing north, which the setbacks take as the front); the street side with the lot's frontage and depth on it; north; the ground (sloped with its fall, read flat, or not read); the address, parcel and zoning when known; whether the lot is only the new-project placeholder; and where the footprint sits now with its yards.

building.description: The building, by its id (list_levels' parentId). Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

site.description: The site, by its id (get_site's siteId), when the scene has several: a lot no building stands on yet reads in site coordinates. Default: the building's site.

name: place_building
title: Place building
description: Stand a building on its site before or after its walls go up. It moves only the building node, so walls, levels and roofs keep their coordinates and move with it. The footprint (outline, the plan you are about to draw, in the coordinates you will draw it; else the walls standing) lands centred in the buildable area, or at the yards a site plan or the person gives. A building with walls keeps its rotation unless rotationDeg is given (get_site's squareRotationDeg squares it to the street); one with none yet is turned square to the street. Fences, paths and plants on its levels move with it.

building.description: The building, by its id (list_levels' parentId). Default: the building of the floor the person is viewing, else the scene's only building.

outline.description: The footprint's corners in order, as [x, z] in metres, in the level coordinates the walls are (or will be) drawn in. Default: the walls standing.

yards.description: Where the house stands instead of centred: at most one of front and rear, and one of left and right, from a site plan or the person. An axis not given stays centred in the buildable area. Needs the site to know its street (frontEdge).

front.description: The front yard: from the lot line to the house, square to the house. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

rear.description: The rear yard: from the lot line to the house, square to the house. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

left.description: The left (seen from the street) yard: from the lot line to the house, square to the house. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

right.description: The right (seen from the street) yard: from the lot line to the house, square to the house. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

rotationDeg.description: The building's rotation about the vertical. Default: the rotation it has, or square to the street while it has no walls. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

name: search_assets
title: Search assets
description: Search the item library (furniture, fixtures, lights, plants, outdoor) by keyword, with one or several queries in a call. The catalog is a limited set that varies by server: what a search returns is what exists. Results provide valid asset ids and placement facts when these are not already known. A query matches the items whose name, id, category or tags hold every one of its words. Returns one group per query, best matches first (the name exactly, then words of the name, words starting it, the category, a tag), at most limit items (24 unless set, up to 60); total counts every match and truncated says the limit cut some, with a hint on how to narrow. Each item has its id, name, category, dimensions [width, height, depth] in metres and attachTo (null on the floor, else 'wall', 'wall-side' or 'ceiling'). Related lookups (sofa, coffee table, tv stand) can share a call.

category.description: Only items of this category (furniture, kitchen, bathroom, outdoor, …).

queries.description: One or more searches to run in a single call.

limit.description: Most items per query, best first; 24 unless set. Narrowing a query beats raising this.

name: view_assets
title: View catalog items
description: Pictures of catalog items by id, each with its size and the names of its paintable surfaces (paint takes one as role).

ids.description: One to six catalog item ids, as search_assets or furnish_room returned them.

name: search_materials
title: Search materials
description: Search or browse the material library (the finishes paint gives), several queries in one call: find a library material's ref here rather than guessing it. The library is Pascal's materials and, in the editor, the ones it holds besides (the community's, yours, your workspace's). A query's words match the words of a material's id, name and kind, or a piece of its id (plank48, cco), building words as the library writes them (timber is wood, weatherboard is siding, render is stucco), colour words by its shade (dark, light, white, grey) and surface words (roof, wall, floor, ceiling) by what it suits; a word of one or two letters, or one as common as 'the', searches nothing. Without a query, a browse lists by name every material of its kind, or that suits its surface (flat colours suit every one), or the whole library. Returns one group per query: each material's ref (library:<id>), name, kind, the surfaces it suits and its colour, best first (a browse by name), 12 at a time for a search and 150 for a browse; the words no material answers (missing), so a finish the library lacks is said, not guessed; and on a long list how many more there are (more) and the offset that lists them (next).

query.description: Search words, e.g. "white render", "grey metal roofing", "oak floor"; leave them out to browse.

surface.description: Only materials that suit this surface; flat colours suit every one.

offset.description: The next page of a long search or browse: the next it returned.

queries.description: One or more searches or browses to run in one call.

name: get_spatial_hierarchy
title: Get spatial hierarchy
description: Read rooms → functional zones → furniture groups → items, with unassigned furniture and issues. All ids come from the scene. Group membership is explicit; ungrouped containment uses plan reference points. Support parentId is separate and unchanged.

name: get_functional_zone_remainder
title: Preview remaining functional-zone area
description: Read-only exact difference: room footprint (excluding room holes) minus the union of existing functional zones. Returns all disjoint parts and holes, areaM2 and empty. When creating a new zone, OMIT excludeId: existing zones must be subtracted. Pass excludeId ONLY for that same existing zone being replaced. edit_functional_zone uses id (not excludeId) for an edit. Coordinates are level-local [x,z] metres; creates nothing. Apply via edit_functional_zone with fillRemaining:true to compute from the latest scene.

name: list_functional_zones
title: List functional zones
description: List independent functional zones inside a room, or all rooms. Returns functions, plan polygons in metres and roomId. These regions never create walls, floors or additional rooms.

name: list_furniture_groups
title: List furniture groups
description: List persisted furniture groups with members, roles, anchors and functionalZoneId. Optional functionalZoneId narrows the list.

name: edit_functional_zone
title: Edit functional zone
description: Create or edit an independent functional zone. Creation needs roomId, name and polygon ([x,z] metres), or fillRemaining:true; edits name id. holes excludes interiors of the primary polygon. parts holds additional disjoint polygon/holes components under the same zone ID. fillRemaining computes room minus the union of the other zones, including holes; it replaces this zone geometry, excluding itself. Preview with get_functional_zone_remainder first. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Each component must be simple and inside the room, excluding room holes; zones may overlap. delete removes zone and group records, preserving furniture. Refuses room_required, outside_room, invalid_polygon.

name: edit_furniture_group
title: Edit furniture group
description: Create or edit a furniture group referencing a functional zone and existing item ids. Creation needs functionalZoneId, name, memberIds. Does not move or reparent furniture. An item belongs to at most one group; members share the room level. Optional anchorNodeId must be a member; null clears it. memberRoles maps member ids to roles. delete removes only the group. Refuses member_already_grouped, item_required, group_level_mismatch.

name: transform_furniture_group
title: Transform furniture group
description: Move by translate [dx,dz] metres and/or rotate by angleDegrees around pivot [x,z]. Positive angles use Pascal Y-axis rotation. Default pivot is the anchor in level space, including its support transforms, else mean root positions. Rotation then translation is one undo step. Only floor roots move; hosted children follow once with local pose and parentId preserved. Refuses external_support for hosted child without its supporting item. Does not reassign membership or solve collisions; inspect hierarchy/issues afterwards.

name: cut_floor_opening
title: Cut floor or ceiling opening
description: Create a persistent opening on a room or level from a polygon or rectangle. A floor cut also opens the automatic ceiling directly below; a ceiling cut can also open the floor above. Use cutsAdjacent:false for a one-surface cut. A mezzanine room cuts only its own plate. levelIds repeats the opening as a shaft on several levels.

width.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

depth.description: In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: remove_floor_opening
title: Remove floor opening
description: Remove an authored floor or ceiling opening and restore the derived surfaces it cut.

name: set_floor_foundation
title: Set floor and foundation
description: Supply slabId or slabIds; grouped plates receive the same floor-top displacement, while edge slots apply only to the first plate. A ground-contact floor has two inputs: thickness (slab, min 0.01 m, grows upward from the foundation) and foundationHeight (0 = on the ground, no foundation; > 0 = raised on a solid foundation; foundation.type "solid" alone raises it 0.3 m, "none" puts it on the ground). The floor top is derived and never floats: grade + foundationHeight + thickness; everything the floor carries (walls, openings, items, rooms, storeys above) moves with the top. Legacy floorHeight (a target top) maps to foundationHeight = top - grade - thickness, never below 0; null = on the ground. On upper plates the underside stays on the walls below: thickness (or floorHeight as a target top) changes the top; only ground-contact plates accept a foundation. Explicit room floors translate with the floor to preserve steps.

thickness.description: Slab thickness in meters. On the ground it sits on the foundation (or the ground) and grows upward: a thicker slab raises the floor top and everything on it. Never below 0.01 m (smaller values are clamped). Upstairs the underside stays on the walls below. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

foundationHeight.description: Ground-bearing floors only: height of the foundation under the slab, in meters. 0 = on the ground (no foundation); > 0 = raised on a solid foundation. The floor top is derived: grade + foundationHeight + thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

name: add_object
title: Build object
description:
Author parametric Three.js furniture, decor and custom objects of any shape, dimensions or style, whether or not the catalog holds something similar (the catalog is a limited set that varies by server). Examples include a low oak table, a slatted bench, a paper lantern, built-ins, custom columns and capitals, mouldings and trim, panels, exposed beams, ceiling bodies, canopies, a porch and railings. Pascal runs the module in a sandbox, stores the result and places it as one object the user can move, paint, and ask you to edit again.

Module shape (import THREE from the three package as usual; the addons below too):
  // also available: three/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js, three/addons/geometries/{RoundedBoxGeometry,ConvexGeometry,LoftGeometry,ParametricGeometry}.js, three-bvh-csg (Brush, Evaluator, SUBTRACTION, ADDITION, INTERSECTION)
  export const params = { width: { default: 4.8, min: 3, max: 8, step: 0.1, unit: 'm', label: 'Width' } }
  export const mount = 'floor'   // 'floor' | 'wall-side' (on a wall face) | 'wall' (through a wall, like a window) | 'ceiling'
  export default function build({ params, THREE }) { const group = new THREE.Group(); /* … */ return group }

One object is one feature that changes together: a table, a bench, a porch, a railing run, a fireplace surround, a ceiling with its beams. Never a whole house, and never walls, rooms, floors, roofs, stairs, doors or windows: those have their own tools. A new object's reason records its design intent: what the authored shape, dimensions or style contributes to the request. The scene check lists every authored object with its reason; no catalog-exhaustion proof is required. On a floor, a plain box with a wall's size or a floor plate is refused with the tool to use (use_walls, use_slab); a detailed object with a wall's size (a bookcase, a screen), or one named after something Pascal builds, is built with a hint naming the tool.

Conventions (they make the object work in Pascal; follow them):
- Metres, Y up, modelled in its installed orientation. Floor and wall mounts put the bottom-centre of the visible bounds at the placement point. Ceiling mounts put the top-centre there: visible geometry extends down in negative local Y, with its top at Y = 0. Wall-side mounts put the bottom-centre of the back face there (back at Z = 0, facing +Z). Normalization translates geometry; it does not flip it.
- Paint: name every material slot_<finish> (slot_trim, slot_frame, slot_metal) and reuse one material per finish; a material named "glass" renders as glass. A slot's colour is shown as the library finish it matches (wood, metal, the nearest flat colour); exact: true keeps each colour as written.
- Parts: name the few groups a person would point at part:<id> (part:column_left, part:canopy, part:landing), usually 2–24, a group per part, not every mesh. Set userData.type on parts someone would look for: column, beam, slab, roof, railing, panel, trim, step, light.
- Lights: add a THREE.PointLight or SpotLight named light:<id> where the bulb is; it becomes a switchable light. A SpotLight keeps its aim (its target), angle and penumbra (a sconce's cone, a recessed downlight). castShadow = true makes it cast shadows (only the couple nearest the view do at once, so keep it for the lights that shape a room). userData.glow = { size, strength } draws a soft halo around the lamp in its colour (size across in metres, about 0.15 for a sconce to 0.4 for a lantern; strength default 1), strongest at dusk and night.
- Motion: put THREE.AnimationClips on the returned group's .animations, as in any three.js project; tracks target <objectName>.<property> or <object.uuid>.<property> and may use any transform property (position, rotation, rotation[y], quaternion, scale); material and visibility tracks do not animate. A clip named open becomes the object's open/close control (close plays a clip named close, or open reversed); a clip named loop runs continuously; every other clip gets its own play toggle labelled with its name (name it for the person: "Twirl", "Music"). Write as many clips as the object needs.
- Cuts: a mesh named cutout cuts only the mounted host; cut:wall, cut:ceiling and cut:slab require that host kind (floor items cut their support slab). The hidden cutter must reach the host; walls use its real shape, ceilings and slabs its through-hole footprint.
- Sockets: an empty Object3D named anchor:<id> marks where other things attach.
- No textures, network or DOM. At most 300k triangles (every instance of an InstancedMesh counts), 32 materials, 60 m per side.

Blender instead (language 'bpy'): when the shape is easier with Blender's modelling (bevelled or rounded edges, subdivision-smooth and organic forms, booleans, curves and text, solidify, array, screw and other modifiers), write a bpy module:
  import bpy, bmesh
  PARAMS = {"width": {"default": 1.8, "min": 1.2, "max": 2.6, "step": 0.05, "unit": "m", "label": "Width"}}
  MOUNT = "floor"
  def build(params): ...   # add objects to the empty scene; everything in it is exported, modifiers applied
The same conventions in Blender terms: metres, Z up, the front faces -Y (Blender's Front view); part:<id>, light:<id> (a point or spot light object; its custom properties intensity sets the brightness, default 2, shadows = True casts shadows, glow = {"size": 0.2, "strength": 1} draws the halo), anchor:<id> (an empty), cutout, cut:wall|ceiling|slab and collider are object names; userData is the object's custom properties (obj["type"] = "panel"); slot_<finish> are material names. A clip is one action named open, close, loop or anything else, assigned to every object that moves in it. Use the data API and bmesh, not operators that need a 3D viewport. A Blender build takes a few seconds.

Several objects: they do not depend on each other, so several add_object calls can go in one step, or in one run_batch call (a call per object; each is reported on its own with its receipt, and one that fails does not stop the others).

From words instead of code: pass piece (what it is in your own words, its size and mount) with name, category and reason. Pascal's own model writes its module in the background under these conventions, compile-checked and repaired, many at a time; the call answers at once with the piece's id and status pending, so go on working. Where the host offers it; each piece spends credits. Given position (or parentId), the object is placed there when its module lands; given neither, it is only made, and author_scene items place it, as many times as they name its id (piece). A piece that fails comes back in author_scene's report.

Edit: pass nodeId with new code and/or params (params alone rebuild the stored script; get_source provides the current code and params when needed); identity, placement, paint and the params you leave out are kept. The result lists the size, parts, slots, lights, animations and params.
