name: author_scene
title: Author scene
description:
Turn a whole design you wrote as free three.js into an editable Pascal scene: the payload holds the whole design. You read your own module however you like (its source, running it and reading the objects, both) and hand over a conversion payload: levels, walls (straight, curved or glass) with their openings, rooms (each naming its unit in a building of several dwellings or tenancies: a condo, an apartment building, a hotel; a room naming none is common area), slabs, voids, columns, railings, stairs, every piece of furniture as an authored object with its own module, and lights. Pascal does the rest server-side: compiles and stores each item, places it, derives the rooms and their floors, paints, runs its checks, saves, and answers with a gate report you iterate against. Nothing you hand over is silently dropped: what cannot be placed comes back by name with a reason, and what Pascal corrected (a wall end snapped onto the centerline it meets) is listed.

Coordinates: metres, plan x/z, Y up, each level's floor at y = 0 in its own frame. A wall is its centerline; walls meet where centerlines meet, so end a partition on the centerline of the wall it runs into. An opening's 'along' is measured from the wall's start to the opening's centre; give each opening its type (how it opens) and style (its look), or its own module for a shape they cannot express. An item's position is where its bottom centre stands, except a ceiling item's (mount 'ceiling': a pendant, a ceiling light): it hangs from the ceiling of the room containing its plan position, its top on that ceiling, and its y is not read. A rug, a mat or a runner is an item lying on the room's floor. What stands on a floor stands on its finish: on a room with a floorCode, on the top of its planks or tiles, so its y stays 0. Its module follows the add_object contract (metres, Y up, built in its installed orientation; at most 300k triangles and 32 materials per item; name materials slot_<finish>; drawers, doors and lids as animation clips; a THREE light named light:<id> where a bulb is: a SpotLight for a cone, castShadow for shadows, userData.glow for a halo). A hex colour is written as an exact material, one per distinct colour. Pascal builds a wall's cap, the floor plate and the ceiling itself: fold a module's caps, underlays and floor planks into the wall, the room's floor finish and the room (say so in notes), never into slabs or regions: baseboards are the wall's skirting, a plank or tile floor is the room's floorCode (a terrace's decking or paving its slab's surfaceCode), tiles, panelling or boards on a wall are its faceLeft / faceRight (or the room's wallCode), cladding, brick or battens outside its faceOutside; a slab is a terrace, a platform, a balcony; a stair is its level's stairs, which open the floor above; the roof over the top level is roof, Pascal's own segments when its shape is one of theirs, else your geometry as roof items, both on the building's roof level above the top storey. Pascal draws what bold architecture needs natively: a curved wall is one wall with the point its arc passes through, through (never a run of short straight ones), a glass front a curtain wall, a double-height room a void in the floor of the level above it (its ceiling opens with it, a railing along its edges), an archway a passage with an arch shape. Paint a wall by what its faces look onto, colorInside and colorOutside: which face is inside is Pascal's to find. Build the building as it is built: a wall at its real height, nothing lowered or removed for viewing.

Hand over the payload, or your module and its adapter, the program that reads the module and returns the payload: Pascal runs the adapter (one that throws comes back with its error, and nothing is written). A payload too large for one call can go by reference: payloadFile names a JSON project file that holds it. An item names its piece instead of code when add_object makes it from words; one still being made is written when it lands, with no call from you. Pieces made from words are written many at a time while you go on, so furniture made that way does not lengthen your turn the way pieces you write yourself do.

One answer has an output limit, and the limit counts thinking and the call's arguments together; answers that planned and wrote a whole house as one payload have stopped there before the payload was complete. The payload is the whole design: a later call with replace: true removes what its payload leaves out, and a call without replace on a scene that holds a conversion is refused (conversion_exists). A conversion stores one module and one adapter, and only when it succeeds; a later call with replace: true and edits (each find text occurring exactly once) changes parts of them, and the adapter runs on the whole edited module. create_room, add_wall, add_door, add_window and create_stair add to the scene a call at a time.

The report says what was written, what Pascal defaulted (defaults: a window with no type is fixed and cannot open), what it warns about but wrote (warnings: thin slabs, too many slabs or regions), what it refused (defects, by your ids), the items waiting for their pieces (pending), and Pascal's checks of what stands (checks, each passed or with what failed: doors and windows a person opens move, glazing is glass, every room's floor covered, every placed piece standing, nothing written as loose debris or buried, wall finishes built, stairs arriving inside a room clear of walls, every level holding rooms or walls: the ground, terraces and foundations belong to the ground level, Pascal draws the site and foundations; where units are named, every room in one or plausibly common).

Call again with replace: true to revise the previous conversion: the module and adapter you leave out are the stored ones, edits change parts of them, and with neither a payload nor a module, adapter or edits the stored conversion is written again. Stable element identities and manual changes are retained; overlapping changes are refused. An existing building without a conversion baseline is never cleared.
A payload by reference is a project file you upload: upload_project_file with phase prepare and its size answers a signedUrl; PUT the bytes there; then phase complete with the returned fileId and storageKey; that fileId is the payloadFile. A server that keeps no project files refuses payloadFile (files_unavailable); one that cannot run an adapter refuses the module and adapter (adapter_unavailable).

payload.description: The conversion payload. Leave it out to have Pascal run the adapter on the module, or, with neither, to write the stored conversion again.

elevation.description: The level's floor height above the ground floor's (default 0), its walking surface. It sets the storey below: a storey is as tall as the climb to the next level's floor (its stairs follow), the top one as its tallest wall; the walls under keep their height and this level's floor fills the climb above them. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Default 0 m.

id.description: Your own id, unique across every wall and item on all levels.

height.description: Wall height, from its floor to its top: the room's height, as built. Under another level, the climb from the tallest wall within 0.5 m of that level's floor up to it is that floor's structure, which Pascal draws (2.7 m walls under a floor at 2.9 m: a 0.2 m floor); a wall reaching into that floor stops under it. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

thickness.description: Wall thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

through.description: [x, z] the point the wall's arc passes through at its middle, bending it from start through it to end (a bay, an apse, a rounded corner, a drum: put it outside the building for one that bulges out): how far it stands from the straight line sets the bend, at most half the start-to-end distance (a half circle). Default: straight. Rooms derive from the arc and openings sit along it; a curved wall takes no faceLeft / faceRight or wallCode, and nothing hangs on it (host). in plan metres.

curtain.description: A curtain wall: glass from the floor to the wall's top between mullions, straight or curved (a glass front, a winter garden). Doors may sit in it; its faces take no paint, skirting or face finish.

spacing.description: The mullions at most this far apart (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 1.5 m.

frameColor.description: The mullions' and frame's colour, #rrggbb or library:<id> (default: Pascal's dark grey).

color.description: Paint for both faces: #rrggbb, written as an exact material, or a library ref (library:<id>) from search_materials.

colorInside.description: Paint for the face or faces that look into a room of this level, same forms as color: both faces of a partition, the room side of an outside wall. Pascal finds them once the rooms are derived and the report says which face it was; over color.

colorOutside.description: Paint for a face no room of this level looks into (an outside wall's cladding or render), same forms as color; over color. Say an outside wall's two finishes this way, not by left and right. The floor between this level and the one above wears the colour most of this level's walls give here, so the facade reads as one.

colorLeft.description: Paint for the face on the left when looking from start to end, same forms as color; over colorInside, colorOutside and color. The left is the wall's front.

colorRight.description: Paint for the face on the right when looking from start to end, same forms as color; over colorInside, colorOutside and color.

sidelightLeft.description: Fixed glazed light left of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sidelightRight.description: Fixed glazed light right of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

transomHeight.description: Fixed light above a swing door and its sidelights, metres; absent or 0 means none. The full cutout must fit under the wall top (wall_too_low). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

slidingStyle.description: Sliding family: patio (default) or two-track bypass closet.

hingesSide.description: Casement or tilt-turn side hinges (default left).

openingDirection.description: Casement or awning swing toward exterior or interior, independent of placement (new windows default outward). Ignored by hopper and tilt-turn, which open inward.

tiltTurnMode.description: Tilt-turn only: tilt inward about the bottom up to 15 degrees (default), or turn inward about the side hinges up to 90 degrees.

rollerShutter.description: Roller mount (default none): box on the exterior face above the opening, or concealed with a 0.03 m lintel strip and 0.025 x 0.03 m guides inside the reveal. Concealed curtain sits 0.02 m outside the frame plane, width minus 0.05 m.

rollerShutterBoxHeight.description: Exterior roller box height (default 0.18 m); used only by the box mount. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rollerShutterOpen.description: Static roller curtain position: 0 down, 1 fully up (default 1), independent of operationState.

shutterOpen.description: Exterior shutter position: 0 closed over the window, 1 open (default 1). Leaves over 0.75 m fold into two stacked halves; narrower leaves open flat against the wall.

shutterSides.description: Which exterior shutter leaves to build (default both).

sillOverhang.description: Exterior sill extension on each side; default 0.4 times sillDepth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sillInteriorDepth.description: Interior stool depth (default 0.06 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorThickness.description: Interior stool thickness (default 0.03 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorOverhang.description: Interior stool extension beyond casing on each side (default 0.015 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

columns.description: Panes across each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal widths; overrides the style's panes.

rows.description: Panes up each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal heights; overrides the style's panes.

windowHandle.description: Show the interior sash handle (default true).

sashGrid.description: Pane grid per operable sash (default false; columns or rows enable it).

sillInterior.description: Add a stool board on the room side (default false).

shutters.description: Exterior shutters (default none), with a 10 mm overlap lip on one leaf when both sides are present.

shutterWidth.description: Width per side, uncapped: defaults to half the opening for both sides, full opening for left or right only. Widths over 0.75 m form a bifold pair of equal halves. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

kind.description: door, window, or passage: a doorway with no leaf (a cased opening, an archway between rooms), which takes no type, style, leaves, hinge, swing or code.

along.description: From the wall's start to the opening's centre, along the centerline (along the arc on a curved wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

width.description: Opening width. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Opening height. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sill.description: Bottom of the opening above the floor the wall stands on; 0 for a door or floor-to-ceiling glazing (default 0). Negative reaches below that floor, down to the wall's bottom where the wall goes down beside a sunken floor: a garage door filling its doorway to a garage floor below the level's. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Default 0 m.

shape.description: Its outline: rectangle (default), rounded top corners, or arch (a round top), for a door, a window or a passage.

archHeight.description: An arch's rise above its straight sides, within height (default 0.45 m for a door or passage, 0.35 m for a window). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

type.description: How it opens. A door: hinged (default), double (two leaves), french (two glazed leaves), folding, pocket, barn, sliding, garage-sectional, garage-rollup, garage-tiltup. A window: fixed (default; cannot open), sliding, casement, awning, hopper, tilt-turn (inward tilt or turn), single-hung, double-hung, bay, bow, louvered. Give it: a window with no type is written fixed.

style.description: Its look, by name. A door's leaf: panel (default), glass, modern, paneled-glass, french, shaker, six-panel, craftsman, half-louvered, barn. A fixed window's panes: single (default), double-hung, triple-hung, casement, sliding, grid, tall-grid, wide-grid, horizontal-bands, transom, picture; an operable window draws its own sashes, so a style on one is dropped and reported.

leaves.description: A door's leaves: sliding 2–4; folding 2, 4, 6 or 8 (default: what its type has; 2 for double, french and sliding).

code.description: A three.js module for an opening type and style cannot express (an arched double door, a round window): the add_door / add_window code contract, mount 'wall', a cutout mesh the wall cuts, an open clip unless it is fixed. Width and height are what it builds; type keeps its meaning (default hinged for a door, fixed for a window), style is ignored. Compiled and stored as an item's module is.

color.description: Exact #rrggbb for a door’s panel and frame or a window’s frame (default: the opening’s own finish).

frameColor.description: Exact #rrggbb for the frame (default: color, or the opening’s own finish when color is absent).

handleStyle.description: Door handle: lever (default), lever-curved, knob, bar, or plate.

hinge.description: Which end of the wall the door's hinge is nearer (default start). The handle goes on the opposite edge.

swing.description: The side the door opens towards: the wall's front or back face.

skirting.description: The wall's skirting (baseboard), native on the wall: it runs along the faces a room stands on, steps with the floor and breaks at doors. Give it here, never as an item.

height.description: Skirting height up the face (default 0.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 0.1 m.

depth.description: How far it stands proud of the face (default 0.012 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 0.012 m.

color.description: #rrggbb, written as an exact material, or library:<id> (default: the skirting's own finish as Pascal draws it).

faceLeft.description: The face on the left looking from start to end (the front, colorLeft's face), built by a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change; colorLeft stays the paint under it. Over the room's wallCode. The report warns when the build leaves part of the face uncovered.

code.description: The face's finish: a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change.

toHeight.description: Where the finish stops, metres up from the face's base (default: the full face). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

faceRight.description: The face on the right looking from start to end (colorRight's face), built by a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change; colorRight stays the paint under it. Over the room's wallCode. The report warns when the build leaves part of the face uncovered.

code.description: The face's finish: a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change.

toHeight.description: Where the finish stops, metres up from the face's base (default: the full face). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

faceOutside.description: The finish of the face no room of this level looks into (an outside wall's cladding, brick, render with bands, battens), built by a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change; colorOutside stays the paint under it. Which face is outside is Pascal's to find, as for colorOutside: both faces of a wall no room stands on. The report warns when the build leaves part of the face uncovered.

code.description: The face's finish: a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change.

toHeight.description: Where the finish stops, metres up from the face's base (default: the full face). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name.description: The room's name as a person would say it (Bedroom 2, Salle de bains, Living + kitchen).

seed.description: [x, z] a point inside the room in plan metres.

floor.description: The floor's material: a library ref (library:<id>) from search_materials, or #rrggbb for an exact flat colour.

floorRegions.description: Parts of the floor in another finish (the kitchen tiles inside an open-plan room), library:<id> or #rrggbb. Regions are fixed polygons that do not follow a resize: one region per finish, never one per plank.

floorCode.description: A three.js module that builds the floor finish for the room's polygon: it receives params.polygon ([[x, z], …]) and params.holes ([[[x, z], …], …]), plan x/z in level coordinates, metres, and lays out the planks, tiles or boards. y = 0 is the floor's surface: lay the finish from there up, and Pascal stands the build on the room's floor plate and what stands on the floor (a rug, a sofa) on the build's top. Pascal cuts the build to the polygon and its holes, so a row may run past the edges (the holes are there for a layout that wants them). Pascal rebuilds it when the room changes; floor stays the fallback finish. The report warns when the build leaves part of the floor uncovered.

wallCode.description: The finish of every wall face that looks into this room (the faces its floor meets, where the skirting runs), each built by a three.js module that builds this face's finish (tiles with joints, panelling, boards) for exactly the face: it receives, in wall-local metres (x along the wall from its start, y up from the face's base, z out of the face), params.outline ({ x0, y0, x1, y1 }: the face), params.holes (its doors and windows, each { x0, y0, x1, y1 }), params.base (the floor along the face, [[x, y], …]) and params.thickness, and lays the finish out: Pascal cuts the build to the outline and its openings, so tiles and boards may run past the edges and over the doors and windows (the holes are there for a layout that wants them, tiles centred on a window); Pascal rebuilds it when the wall or its openings change. A wall's own faceLeft / faceRight wins over it. The report warns when the build leaves part of a face uncovered.

wallToHeight.description: Where the room's wallCode stops, metres up from the face's base (default: the full face). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

unit.description: The unit this room belongs to, by name (Apartment 2B, Suite 301): a dwelling, hotel room or commercial lot of a building with several; rooms with no unit are common area (corridor, lobby, stairs). Leave it out in a single-family house.

thickness.description: Slab thickness (default 0.15 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 0.15 m.

top.description: The slab's top above the level's floor; a balcony at 0, a plinth below 0 (default 0). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Default 0 m.

surfaceCode.description: A three.js module that builds the slab's surface finish (a terrace's decking or paving, a platform's boards): it receives params.polygon ([[x, z], …]) and params.holes ([[[x, z], …], …]), the slab's outline in level plan x/z, metres, and lays the boards or slabs out from y = 0, the slab's top. Pascal cuts the build to the polygon and its holes, so a row may run past the edges, and stands what is placed on the slab on the build's top. Pascal rebuilds it when the slab changes; finish stays the fallback and the sides keep theirs. The report warns when the build leaves part of the slab uncovered.

railing.description: Railing runs standing on this slab (a balcony).

height.description: Railing height (default 1.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 1.1 m.

voids.description: Openings in this level’s floor onto the level below; never on the first level.

polygon.description: The opening in this level's floor, so the room below rises through it (a double-height living room under a gallery, a stairwell, an atrium). Pascal cuts the floor and the ceiling under it, and stops the cut at the faces of this level's walls.

railing.description: A railing along the void's open edges, broken where a wall of this level stands or a stair arrives (default: a 1.1 m railing; null for none, a void you cannot walk up to).

height.description: Railing height (default 1.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 1.1 m.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical axis (default 0): at 0 its width runs along x. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Default 0°.

shape.description: square (default), or round: width is its diameter and depth is not read.

width.description: Column width. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

depth.description: Column depth (default: its width). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Column height. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

color.description: Its finish, #rrggbb written as an exact material, or library:<id> (default: Pascal's plaster). A column built by code keeps its module's colours.

code.description: A three.js module for a column shape and width cannot express (a timber post with brackets, a fluted or tapered pier, a steel section): the add_column code contract, mount 'floor', built standing from y = 0 with its bottom centre on position; what it builds sets its width, depth and height, so shape, width, depth and height are not read. Compiled and stored as an item's module is.

stairs.description: Stairs rising from this level to the next one in levels, as Pascal's stair tool builds them: the risers follow the storey height and each stair opens the floor above over its flights. Never a stair as an item.

start.description: [x, z] the middle of the bottom step's front edge, where the climb starts in plan metres.

rotation.description: Which way the first flight climbs: 0 toward +z, 90 toward +x, 180 toward −z, 270 toward −x (default 0). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Default 0°.

width.description: Width across the climb (default 1.0 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m. Default 1 m.

layout.description: straight (default); l: a flight, a landing as deep as the stair is wide, a flight turned 90°; u: a flight, a landing across, a flight back beside the first.

turn.description: Which way an L or U turns, to the climber's left or right (default left).

length.description: The flights' run along the climb, landings aside (default: 0.28 m of going per riser, risers of at most 0.18 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

steps.description: Risers in all (default: from the storey, risers of at most 0.18 m).

lowerSteps.description: An L or U's risers up to its landing; the rest climb after it (default half).

railing.description: Which sides have a railing, looking up the flight (default both): none, left, right or both.

railingStyle.description: How the railings are built (default balusters): post-and-rail, cable, boards, glass or metal.

color.description: The flight's finish, treads and body, #rrggbb written as an exact material, or library:<id> (default: wood treads on a light grey body).

treads.description: The treads' finish, over color; same forms.

id.description: Your own id, for the report and for hosting.

category.description: One word a catalog would use: bed, chair, sofa, plant, lamp, sink.

code.description: The piece's own three.js module (see the description); or piece.

piece.description: Instead of code: the id of a piece add_object makes from words (its piece.id). Placed with its module once made; one still being made is placed when it lands.

position.description: [x, y, z] bottom centre (a ceiling item's top centre, y not read) in metres, y above the level's floor.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical axis (default 0). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Default 0°.

host.description: The id of the item this one rests on or hangs from (a lamp on a nightstand), or of the wall it is fixed to (a baseboard, a casing, a mirror, art), so moving the host moves it. On a wall, position is still the world bottom centre: the item faces the room on the nearest face, keeping its outward distance from that face; a point inside the wall moves to the face and is reported. Rotation is ignored.

lights.description: This level's lights (default []): each in its fixture, or on a ceiling point Pascal adds.

position.description: [x, y, z] the bulb in metres, y above the level's floor.

intensity.description: Relative brightness, 1 for an ordinary bulb (default 1).

fixture.description: The id of the item holding this light (a pendant, a lamp). Default: without a fixture, a minimal ceiling point is created on the ceiling of the room containing the light’s plan position; outside any room, it attaches to the nearest item on this level and reports the fallback.

direction.description: Makes it a spotlight pointing this way, [x, y, z] (any length): [0, -1, 0] straight down (a recessed downlight), [0, 1, 0] up a wall (a sconce washing upwards).

target.description: [x, y, z] a point a spotlight aims at, instead of direction in metres, y above the level's floor.

angle.description: A spotlight's full cone (default 60): about 30 for a narrow accent, 60 for a downlight, 100 for a wide wash. Giving it makes the light a spot pointing down unless direction or target says otherwise. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Range 1–179 deg.

softness.description: How feathered a spotlight's edge is: 0 hard, 1 fully soft (default 0.4).

shadows.description: Casts shadows (default false). Only the couple of shadow-casting lights nearest the view get shadows at once, so keep it for the lights that shape a room.

glow.description: A soft halo drawn around the lamp itself in the light's colour, strongest at dusk and night.

size.description: Across, about 0.15 for a sconce to 0.4 for a lantern. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

units.description: The units the rooms name, to give them a kind or a colour (default []): a unit named only by rooms is an apartment. A unit's rooms may be on several levels (a duplex). Pascal makes one unit per distinct name, under the building, holding the rooms that name it.

name.description: The name the rooms give as their unit.

kind.description: What the unit is: apartment (a dwelling: a flat, a condo, one side of a duplex), hotel-room (a suite or guest room), commercial (a shop, an office, a lot let on its own), common (shared space grouped on purpose). Default apartment.

color.description: #rrggbb tint of the unit in the plan.

roof.description: The roof over the top level, on the building's roof level above it, so exploded and solo level views lift it off the plan.

segments.description: Pascal's own roof over the top level, one segment per rectangle: it stands on the walls' tops and draws its own gable ends, eaves and fascia (default []).

center.description: [x, z] its centre, between the walls it covers in plan metres.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical axis, as an item turns: at 0 its width runs along x. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Default 0°.

width.description: Along its ridge, between the centerlines of the walls under it (a gable's rakes are its ends). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

depth.description: Across its ridge, between the centerlines of the walls under it (its eaves' sides). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

roofType.description: gable (default), hip, shed (one slope, its low eave toward its local +z), flat, or any of the roof shapes create_roof takes.

pitch.description: Slope of its planes (default 40°). In degrees, or rise over run ("6:12"). Range 0–85 deg.

overhang.description: How far its eaves reach past the walls' faces, in plan (default 0.3 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Default 0.3 m.

gableOverhang.description: How far a gable's or shed's rakes reach past its end walls, in plan. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

wallColor.description: #rrggbb of the walls the segments raise: their gable ends.

items.description: Roof geometry the segments cannot draw (a roof of another shape, a chimney, a dormer), as items on the roof level. position's y is measured from the top level's floor, as that level's items are.

id.description: Your own id, for the report and for hosting.

category.description: One word a catalog would use: bed, chair, sofa, plant, lamp, sink.

code.description: The piece's own three.js module (see the description); or piece.

piece.description: Instead of code: the id of a piece add_object makes from words (its piece.id). Placed with its module once made; one still being made is placed when it lands.

position.description: [x, y, z] bottom centre (a ceiling item's top centre, y not read) in metres, y above the level's floor.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical axis (default 0). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Default 0°.

host.description: The id of the item this one rests on or hangs from (a lamp on a nightstand), or of the wall it is fixed to (a baseboard, a casing, a mirror, art), so moving the host moves it. On a wall, position is still the world bottom centre: the item faces the room on the nearest face, keeping its outward distance from that face; a point inside the wall moves to the face and is reported. Rotation is ignored.

notes.description: What you could not convert, or converted with a change, one sentence each. Kept with the scene.

payloadFile.description: The payload by reference: the fileId of a JSON project file holding it, from upload_project_file. Instead of payload, for one too large to send in a call.

module.description: The three.js module the payload is read from. Stored with the scene as its source; left out, the stored one is used.

adapter.description: The program that turns the module into the payload: `export default async function adapt({ THREE, addons, source, run, toModule })` returning the payload. Pascal runs it where three.js modules run (no network, files or DOM); source is the module's text, run(code = source) builds a module (its default or named build({ THREE, scene, addons })) and answers { scene }, its world matrices updated; toModule(object, { origin, rotation, mount, animations }) writes an object of the built scene as an item's or an opening's module, answering { code, position, size, triangles }. Stored with the scene; left out, the stored one is used.

edits.description: Changes to the module or the adapter as given, or as stored when left out, applied in order; the changed texts are run and stored.

find.description: Text that occurs exactly once in it.

replace.description: Apply a new design delta to the previous conversion, preserving manual edits (default false).

buildingId.description: The building to convert into. Required when there are several and no active level selects one.

sceneId.description: The scene to write; the active one when omitted.

name: get_source
title: Read object script
description: Read the code module a scripted node runs and return it with its language (three.js or Blender bpy) and its params at their current values. It reads the module of an object, or of a window, door or column built from code; a room's id reads its floor script, the module that builds its floor finish; a slab's id reads its surface script, the module that builds its top's finish; a wall's id with face reads that face's script (face may be left out when only one face has one). Optional source evidence when the current module is needed. An edited module can be passed back with the same nodeId: to add_object for an object, to add_window / add_door / add_column for their respective kinds.

nodeId.description: An object, window, door or column built from code, a room with a floor script, a slab with a surface script, or a wall with a face script.

face.description: A wall's face whose script to read; needed when both faces have one.

name: measure
title: Measure
description: Measure the distance (in meters) between two nodes, or the net area of a polygon node when fromId === toId. Distance is between world-space reference points, returned as fromPoint/toPoint: a positioned node's origin in its host's frame (an item's base, a door's or window's centre in its wall), a wall's or fence's midpoint at its base, a slab's, ceiling's or zone's polygon centroid on its plane, a block's or imported mesh's vertex-bounds centre, a level's plan centre on its base plane, and another container's descendants' centre. `approximate` lists nodes whose renderer derives the pose from data not modelled here (a downspout at its gutter outlet, a gutter at the eave), with the reason.

name: view_scene
title: Look at the scene
description:
Look at the building in 3D from a viewpoint you pick and get the picture back: the finished house, every storey and the roof by default, or an explicit Solo/Exploded level presentation, whatever view mode the person has on. Use it to compare what you built with a reference and say what differs before you fix it: the facade from the photo's own camera (camera: its position, aim, field of view and aspect), rendered at the photo's aspect to lay beside it; or from the photo's side at street height (from 'street', 'street-left', …, eyeHeight 1.7), in its light (lighting); one face square on (projection orthographic); the massing from above, or an aerial view (elevation 40). The view frames the target (a building, a level, a wall or a zone; the whole building, its roof included, by default) from outside, unless you place the eye yourself with position or camera. To stand inside a room and see its furniture and finishes at a person's height, give interior {zoneId} (a room: an id from get_zones or create_room): the eye stands in the room a step in from a corner, looking across it, with the cut below; from picks the side of the room it stands on, target something in the room to look at it. To see inside a floor, give interior {levelId}: the other floors and that floor's roofs and ceilings are left out of the picture, and everything on it, walls, openings and furniture alike, is cut at 0.65 of the storey's height (about two thirds), so a tall wardrobe or a door head is cut, not short; a roof level has no inside; with no eye given it looks down into the floor, or into the room or zone you target. A level below grade, targeted alone, is looked into the same way (from outside the ground would cover it), the ground over it drawn as a faint veil. The live view is not changed. A door, a window or an item on a floor frames at detail scale, an opening seen from its outside face: a close-up to lay beside the photo's crop of the same element, to see what differs. Where the host keeps the picture it answers its viewId: name it to use that exact frame later (a Studio render of this view) without taking it again. A picture is not a measure: take sizes and counts from the tools.
The MCP has no renderer of its own: an editor open on the project renders the picture, the user's own tab or, where the host offers one, an editor on its servers (each view it renders costs credits). A refusal says what to do: editor_tab_required (no editor can render it), editor_tab_hidden (the user's tab is in the background: it must be brought to the front), editor_tab_busy (a tab is open but busy or still loading: call view_scene again in a few seconds, the user need not be asked).

target.description: A building, level, wall, zone, door, window or floor item id to frame. Default: every storey in the scene, walls and roofs.

interior.description: Look inside, with one of: levelId (a floor): the other floors and its roofs and ceilings are left out of the picture, everything on it (walls, openings, furniture) cut at 0.65 of the storey height. Default framing looks down into it; camera or position still wins. zoneId (a room: an id from get_zones or create_room): the same cut, and the eye stands inside the room at a person's height (1.6 m, or eyeHeight), a step in from its corner farthest from what it looks at (from picks the corner on that side), looking across the room with a 75 degree field of view (fov changes it); with a target on the floor it looks at the target. position, elevation, from above or projection orthographic put the eye outside again, over the cut room.

presentation.description: Verify the actual level presentation: stacked (default), exploded, or solo with a levelId. Solo keeps full-height geometry, including ceilings and any roofs incorrectly owned by that floor; it is not the clipped interior view. Does not change the live view. Do not combine with interior.

from.description: The side the eye stands on: a compass side (north is the plan's top edge, z grows south, x east), above, or a side as a front photo names it, standing in the street facing the house ('street-left' is its left front corner, 'back' the far side), from the street the site records, else the house's own front (its -z, the way a generated house faces). Default south-west.

elevation.description: Degrees above the horizon the eye looks down from: 35 to 60 for an aerial view. Default 12. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Range -10–89 deg.

eyeHeight.description: Metres above the ground for a street view (1.7), instead of elevation. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

position.description: The eye exactly, [x, height, z] in metres; it looks at the target.

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees for a perspective view. Default 45. In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Range 10–100 deg.

projection.description: orthographic for a square-on elevation of a face, no perspective.

camera.description: A photo's camera (position, target, fov, aspect): the render takes its eye, aim and field of view at the photo's aspect. Or 'current': the person's own view, as their editor shows it now (the MCP has none: no_current_camera). Not with from, position, elevation, eyeHeight, fov or projection.

fov.description: In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad"). Range 5–120 deg.

lighting.description: The light the picture is rendered in: the scene's own (current, the default), or day, overcast, sunset, dusk (twilight, the lights on) or night, as a reference photo was taken in.

maxPx.description: The picture's longest side in pixels, for a smaller one. Default 1920 by 1200, and never longer than 1920.

photo.description: The photo's crop of the element the view frames, returned beside it in the same call: a door's glass, a lamp's shape, a window's panes, at detail scale, to say what differs.

source.description: The photo as a data:image/...;base64 URL (read the file and encode it); in the chat, the URL of a file the user attached works too.

region.description: [left, top, right, bottom] in the photo's pixels: the element to compare.

name: create_story_shell
title: Create story shell
description: Create one level-owned building shell from a footprint: the perimeter walls. The floor plate and the ceiling are DERIVED from the rooms the walls enclose — never author a slab or a ceiling here, and never pass boundary/autoFromWalls; createSlab / createCeiling / slabElevation are recorded as room intent instead. Use once per story; do not make first-floor walls span multiple stories.

wallHeight.description: Explicit wall height override. Omit for level-plane-bound walls. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Wall thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

createSlab.description: Floor intent for the rooms inside the shell. False records hasFloor: false.

createCeiling.description: Ceiling intent for the rooms inside the shell. False records hasCeiling: false.

slabElevation.description: Walking surface of the derived plate, stored as the room's floor elevation. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

ceilingHeight.description: Ceiling height. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: add_door
title: Add door
description: Add a door to an existing straight wall at t (0..1 along it), or a passage with no leaf (openingKind opening: a cased opening, an arch). The door slides to stay on the wall and reports clamped. On a railing (wallType railing) it is a gap in the guard as tall as the railing, with no leaf, casing or threshold. Refused with a code, as in the editor: curved walls, walls shorter than the door, and overlapping another door, window or wall item unless force is set. Match the reference with the outline (rectangle, rounded, arch), doorType and style; what they cannot express (glass strips, a pattern of lites, carved panels) is written as a script in code, never left as not possible. Not available in run_batch: the host opening executor prepares scripted creation and rebuilds, which a batch does not prepare.

wallId.description: The wall to add the door to.

nodeId.description: Rebuild this door instead of adding one: new code and/or params (get_source provides current code when needed). Its native fields change with update_node.

t.description: Position along the wall, 0..1: 0 = start, 0.5 = centre, 1 = end.

force.description: Place it even where it overlaps another door, window or wall item, like holding Alt in the editor. Only when the person asks for the overlap.

sidelightLeft.description: Fixed glazed light left of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sidelightRight.description: Fixed glazed light right of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

transomHeight.description: Fixed light above a swing door and its sidelights, metres; absent or 0 means none. The full cutout must fit under the wall top (wall_too_low). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

slidingStyle.description: Sliding family: patio (default) or two-track bypass closet.

width.description: Door width (default 0.9 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Door height (default 2.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Rarely needed: the door's bottom above the floor the wall stands on (default 0, on the floor). Negative reaches below that floor, down to the wall's bottom, where the wall goes down beside a floor sunk under it (a garage below the house, a step in the terrain): a garage door filling its doorway down to the garage floor. It stays between the wall's bottom and its ceiling, and reports clamped. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

openingKind.description: door (default), or opening: a passage with no leaf, framed or arched by the outline, as the editor's door panel offers.

handleStyle.description: Door handle: lever (default), lever-curved, knob, bar, or plate.

swingDirection.description: Which way the door opens (default inward).

openingShape.description: Outline of the opening: rectangle (default), rounded top corners, or arch (round top).

archHeight.description: Rise of the arch above its straight sides, within height (arch only; default 0.45 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

cornerRadius.description: Radius of the rounded top corners (rounded only; default 0.15 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

code.description: An optional module (three.js, or bpy with language) for a door (a fan grille, tracery, carved trim): the same module and conventions as add_object, with mount 'wall'. Its size is what it builds (name params width and height so the door's size controls edit them), and its cutout mesh cuts the wall. Make it open like a real door: add an `open` clip (the leaves swinging or sliding; `close` is optional, `open` reversed by default) unless it is fixed. Native fields and code are available to express the requested shape.

language.description: The code's language: 'three' (default) for a three.js module, 'bpy' for a Blender module (see add_object). On an edit it defaults to the language the object was built in.

params.description: Values for the params the module declares; on an edit, each one you leave out keeps its current value (clamped to the param's range) and a param new to the code starts at its default.

name.description: What the user would call this design.

description.description: A short description of this design, at most 200 characters.

category.description: What this design is, in one or two words.

tags.description: Up to five short lowercase search tags, at most 32 characters each.

doorType.description: How it opens (default hinged); garage types for garage doors.

style.description: Visual preset (panels only, never the size); same presets as create_room doors[].

name: add_window
title: Add window
description: Add a window to an existing straight wall at t (0..1 along it), centred vertically on the wall, or on sillHeight above the floor when given. It slides to stay on the wall and under the wall's ceiling, and reports clamped. Refused with a code, as in the editor: curved walls, railings (railing_window: a railing takes a door, a gap in its guard), walls shorter than the window, overlapping another door, window or wall item unless force is set, and a style on a window that is not Fixed (style_needs_fixed_window). Match the reference with the outline (rectangle, rounded, arch), windowType and panes (columns × rows, or a style); what they cannot express (glass strips, leaded lites, a feature frame) is written as a script in code, never left as not possible. Not available in run_batch: the host opening executor prepares scripted creation and rebuilds, which a batch does not prepare.

wallId.description: The wall to add the window to.

nodeId.description: Rebuild this window instead of adding one: new code and/or params (get_source provides current code when needed). Its native fields change with update_node.

t.description: Position along the wall, 0..1: 0 = start, 0.5 = centre, 1 = end.

force.description: Place it even where it overlaps another door, window or wall item, like holding Alt in the editor. Only when the person asks for the overlap.

width.description: Window width (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

openingShape.description: Outline of the opening: rectangle (default), rounded top corners, or arch (round top).

archHeight.description: Rise of the arch above its straight sides, within height (arch only; default 0.35 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

cornerRadius.description: Radius of the rounded top corners (rounded only; default 0.15 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

code.description: An optional module (three.js, or bpy with language) for a window (a fan grille, tracery, carved trim): the same module and conventions as add_object, with mount 'wall'. Its size is what it builds (name params width and height so the window's size controls edit them), and its cutout mesh cuts the wall. Make it open like a real window: add an `open` clip (the sash sliding or swinging; `close` is optional, `open` reversed by default) unless it is fixed. Native fields and code are available to express the requested shape.

language.description: The code's language: 'three' (default) for a three.js module, 'bpy' for a Blender module (see add_object). On an edit it defaults to the language the object was built in.

params.description: Values for the params the module declares; on an edit, each one you leave out keeps its current value (clamped to the param's range) and a param new to the code starts at its default.

name.description: What the user would call this design.

description.description: A short description of this design, at most 200 characters.

category.description: What this design is, in one or two words.

tags.description: Up to five short lowercase search tags, at most 32 characters each.

hingesSide.description: Casement or tilt-turn side hinges (default left).

openingDirection.description: Casement or awning swing toward exterior or interior, independent of placement (new windows default outward). Ignored by hopper and tilt-turn, which open inward.

tiltTurnMode.description: Tilt-turn only: tilt inward about the bottom up to 15 degrees (default), or turn inward about the side hinges up to 90 degrees.

rollerShutter.description: Roller mount (default none): box on the exterior face above the opening, or concealed with a 0.03 m lintel strip and 0.025 x 0.03 m guides inside the reveal. Concealed curtain sits 0.02 m outside the frame plane, width minus 0.05 m.

rollerShutterBoxHeight.description: Exterior roller box height (default 0.18 m); used only by the box mount. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rollerShutterOpen.description: Static roller curtain position: 0 down, 1 fully up (default 1), independent of operationState.

shutterOpen.description: Exterior shutter position: 0 closed over the window, 1 open (default 1). Leaves over 0.75 m fold into two stacked halves; narrower leaves open flat against the wall.

shutterSides.description: Which exterior shutter leaves to build (default both).

sillOverhang.description: Exterior sill extension on each side; default 0.4 times sillDepth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sillInteriorDepth.description: Interior stool depth (default 0.06 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorThickness.description: Interior stool thickness (default 0.03 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorOverhang.description: Interior stool extension beyond casing on each side (default 0.015 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

columns.description: Panes across each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal widths; overrides the style's panes.

rows.description: Panes up each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal heights; overrides the style's panes.

windowHandle.description: Show the interior sash handle (default true).

sashGrid.description: Pane grid per operable sash (default false; columns or rows enable it).

sillInterior.description: Add a stool board on the room side (default false).

shutters.description: Exterior shutters (default none), with a 10 mm overlap lip on one leaf when both sides are present.

shutterWidth.description: Width per side, uncapped: defaults to half the opening for both sides, full opening for left or right only. Widths over 0.75 m form a bifold pair of equal halves. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

style.description: Visual preset of a Fixed window's panes (never the size); same presets as create_room windows[]. Fixed windows only: an operable window draws its own sashes.

name: apply_patch
title: Apply patch
description: Apply a batch of create/update/delete operations atomically. All patches are validated before any are applied; the entire batch forms a single undo step. Batch-first is the default: prefer one apply_patch call containing all create/update/delete ops for a build step, in stable order so later ops can reference ids created by earlier ops. A single call is atomic (all or nothing) and pays the snapshot and save cost once; do not loop one-op calls. A create whose id already exists fails the whole patch with node_exists; to replace a node, delete it earlier in the same patch. An update cannot change id or type (identity_change) or object or children (immutable_field); restating the current value is fine. A parentId change must name an existing node that holds children and cannot point to the node or one of its descendants (invalid_parent). An update cannot add schema issues to a node (invalid_update). After a delete or a roof update that regenerates a roof's default gutters, those gutters and their downspouts are addressable only in a later call (regenerated_default). A roof created or moved onto the storey whose walls carry it goes to the level above them (the roof level over a top storey), said in notes; storey content (walls, zones, slabs, ceilings, items, stairs) on a roof level (roof_level), a walled level declared the roof level (roof_level_holds_storey) and floor indexes putting a roof level under a storey (roof_level_on_top) are refused. Refusals come back as a tool error whose text is JSON {code, patchIndex, id, message}.

name: clear_scene
title: Clear the project
description: Empty the project on purpose, back to the default scaffold: a site, a building and one level of the standard storey height. It is the only way to empty a project: a write that would empty it is refused (scene_wipe_blocked), since that is far more often an accident. Call it only when the person asked to start over, and say what they asked in reason.

reason.description: What the person asked for, in their words.

name: set_zone
title: Set zone
description: Create a polygonal zone on the given level. label is stored as the zone name and properties are merged into metadata. A polygon along walls that already enclose a room is that room, never a second zone: a room still named "Room N", or already named label, takes the label and properties; a room a person named otherwise is refused (rename it with update_node only when the person asked).

name: undo
title: Undo
description: Undo the most recent N steps in the scene history (default 1). Returns the number of steps actually undone.

name: redo
title: Redo
description: Redo the next N previously-undone steps (default 1). Returns the number of steps actually redone.

name: export_json
title: Export JSON
description: Return the scene as a serialized JSON string. Pass `pretty: true` to indent with 2 spaces.

name: export_glb
title: Export GLB
description: Export the scene through the host Three.js renderer when configured. A headless host without a renderer returns a structured not_implemented error.

name: check_collisions
title: Check collisions
description: Assess declared item footprints with a rotation-aware plan AABB test. Supports an explicit minimum clearance and reports units, source dimensions, skipped evidence, and unsupported checks. Optionally scope to one level or floor-standing items.

minimumClearance.description: Minimum free plan-space required between item footprints. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

floorOnly.description: When true, wall-, wall-side-, and ceiling-attached items are excluded.

candidate.description: Read-only prospective furniture item. It is checked against the target level but never added to the scene.

items.description: Candidate position coordinate. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").
Candidate declared size. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rotationY.description: Candidate yaw around the vertical axis. In radians, or text with a unit ("90°").

name: list_templates
title: List scene templates
description: List the seed Pascal scene templates available to `create_from_template`. Returns the id, display name, one-line description and node count for each.

name: create_from_template
title: Create scene from template
description: Instantiate a seed Pascal scene template into the bridge. Regenerates all ids before applying. When `save: true` and a SceneStore is wired, also persists the new scene and returns the SceneMeta.

name.description: Optional display name for the saved scene. Defaults to the template name.

name: create_house_from_brief
title: Create house from brief
description: Replace the session's scene with a starter template and save it as an unpublished draft, returning its editor URL. The template follows bedroomCount, rooms and landscaping only: garden-house for landscaping or a garden, patio or yard room, else empty-studio up to one bedroom, two-bedroom for two and garden-house for more. brief, style and constraints neither choose nor shape it; the summary repeats brief. It saves into projectId's project, or a new one named projectName or after the template; with no scene store it saves nothing. Refine it with the semantic tools afterward.

name: create_project
title: Create project
description: Create a browser-visible Pascal project for the authenticated user. Use this before save_scene when the user asks for a new project.

name: get_project_status
title: Get project status
description: Authoritative status/debug call for a Pascal project: editor URL, browser-visible version, latest saved version, published version, node count, and graph hash.

name: save_scene
title: Save scene
description: Save the current scene (or a provided graph) to the SceneStore. Without id or projectId it saves to the project this session is bound to (create_project or load_scene). Defaults to a browser-visible draft save so agents can iterate without creating many project versions. Use saveMode: "checkpoint" for meaningful version history.

replace.description: Write this session's scene over a project or scene it was not loaded from, replacing what that one holds.

saveMode.description: `draft` updates the browser-visible working model without polluting version history. `checkpoint` creates a meaningful saved version; it does not publish.

publish.description: Hosted Pascal: also publish this checkpoint, making it the version the project's viewers see. Only when the user asks to publish.

includeCurrentScene.description: If true, save the bridge current scene. If false, use the graph arg.

graph.description: Full SceneGraph { nodes, rootNodeIds, collections? } to save instead of the bridge state. Judged against the scene it is saved over (the session's scene when the save goes to it, else the stored scene `id` names) as apply_patch is: a roof it puts on the walls of the storey holding it goes to the level above them, said in notes, and storey content on a roof level is refused. A graph with no scene under it is saved as it is.

name: load_scene
title: Load scene
description: Load a scene from the SceneStore into the bridge. Returns the scene metadata. Throws `scene_not_found` if the id does not exist.

name: list_scenes
title: List scenes
description: List scenes in the SceneStore. Optionally filter by `projectId` and cap results with `limit` (default 100).

name: delete_scene
title: Delete scene
description: Remove a stored scene by id. In Pascal this never deletes the project: it hides it from Pascal's public listings until it is next saved with content, and answers `deleted: false, hidden: true` with a message; its owner can delete it from the projects page. Only someone who can manage the project may hide it. A local scene store deletes the scene. Optionally pass `expectedVersion` for optimistic concurrency.

name: rename_scene
title: Rename scene
description: Rename a scene in the SceneStore. Returns the updated SceneMeta. Optionally pass `expectedVersion` for optimistic concurrency.

name: generate_variants
title: Generate variants
description: Generate N variations of a base scene by forking and applying seeded mutations. Example: "give me 5 variations of this kitchen". If `save=true`, each variant is persisted via scene operations and returned with an id + URL; otherwise the graph is returned inline.

baseSceneId.description: If set, fork from this saved scene; else fork from current bridge state.

save.description: If true, also save each variant via SceneStore and return ids.

name: photo_to_scene
title: Photo to Pascal scene
description: Orchestrator: analyse a floor-plan photo via MCP sampling, translate the structured vision result into a Pascal SceneGraph (site → building → level with walls and zones), optionally save it, and swap the bridge to the new scene. Requires host support for sampling.

image.description: Base64 or https URL of the floor-plan photo

defaultWallThickness.description: Default wall thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

defaultWallHeight.description: Default wall height. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: analyze_floorplan_image
title: Analyze floor-plan image
description: Defer to the MCP host (via sampling) to extract walls, rooms, and approximate dimensions from a floor-plan image. Requires host support for sampling.

scaleHint.description: Text hint about scale, e.g. '1 cm = 1 m' or 'approximately 80 m²'

name: analyze_room_photo
title: Analyze room photo
description: Defer to the MCP host (via sampling) to extract approximate dimensions, fixtures, and windows from a single-room photograph. Requires host support for sampling.
